### ⭐ FRAME POINTERS, on every function — decided at P1.0d.3, but the forcing reason is **P1.5**

**shv2 now emits `push rbp` / `mov rbp, rsp` in EVERY prologue, leaves included** (user decision,
2026-07-15). It previously used frame-pointer-omitted (rsp-only) frames **while still reserving rbp** —
a **strictly dominated** state: it paid the register cost and took none of the benefit. **rbp stays
NON-allocatable; the pool is unchanged at 14.** Addressing stays **rsp-relative** — the divergence from
v1 is deliberate and narrow: **rbp is for the CHAIN, not for addressing.**

**The stack trace only EXPOSED this. The reason it is not a P1.0d.3 detail is
[`__gt_morestack`](maxon-selfhosted/Compiler/Targets/X64/X64Backend.maxon#L7094):** v1 grows a green-thread
stack by allocating 2×, copying, and then **FIXING THE SAVED-RBP CHAIN by the relocation offset** (step 6b
walks the chain on the new stack, adjusting every saved rbp in the old range). GT stacks are 2 KB initial
and **RELOCATE** on growth, Go-`runtime.morestack`-style. ⇒ **A relocating stack must find and fix every
interior frame pointer, and the chain is how it finds them.** **R3 @ P1.5 commits shv2 to exactly that
model**, so shv2 needs frame pointers there *regardless of panics*. Landing them now moved all 279 goldens
**once**; retrofitting at P1.5 moves the same goldens **then**, onto a shipped runtime. *Do the hard things
early.*

⚠ **A frameless leaf could not be spared:** you cannot unwind OUT of one without knowing its frame layout,
and the faulting `main` **is** one — so framing only "framed" functions does not help. (And because no shv2
function ever wrote rbp, rbp was *invariant program-wide*: walking `[rbp]` gave garbage, not a short trace.)
**`.pdata`/`.xdata` + `RtlVirtualUnwind` is the FPO-correct alternative and was rejected: NO compiler in
this tree emits unwind info**, so it has no port source and is its own rung — and it does **not** solve
morestack's fixup, which needs the chain anyway.

⇒ **P1.0d lands before P1.1**, and it pulls the **declaration half of P1.9 forward** (parse + resolve a
top-level ranged `typealias`; the corpus's ranges are wide, so the *checks* — `ExpandCastRangeChecks` /
`InsertRangeChecks` — stay at P1.9 where they belong). Floats need a whole new register bank (there is
**no XMM class** in the allocator today), so they are the last slice of the rung, not the first.

> ### ⭐ P1.2 — two decisions taken elsewhere that land HERE (2026-07-15)
>
> **1. `String.toByteArray()` is a MOVE, and the source is not mutable afterwards** (user decision).
> This is an OWNERSHIP statement, which is why it belongs to this rung and not to the bootstrap's
> refcounting. It **dissolves** a problem rather than managing it: with one owner there is no second
> observer to keep consistent, so there is no aliasing question, **no copy-on-write**, and no
> "independent value" contract to enforce.
>
> The bootstrap cannot do this — it has no ownership — so it takes the fallback: `toByteArray()` returns
> an **independent** ByteArray, implemented as a COW view (`185351d1f`). **That is a stopgap for a
> compiler without moves, not a design to port.** Two of its specs
> (`specs/string-type-2` / `tobytearray-is-independent-of-an-owned-source`,
> `tobytearray-survives-the-source-growing`) **use the string AFTER `toByteArray()` and must become
> use-after-move ERRORS here.** Delete them at this rung with that reason, do not make them pass.
>
> The bootstrap's COW is also **one-directional** — a write through the source's raw `managed` shows
> through a view that has not detached yet (measured). Moves make that unrepresentable. **Do not port
> the COW view, and do not port the hole.**
>
> **2. ⚠ v1's two-result-capture MISCOMPILE is waiting for THIS allocator.** shv2's register allocator is
> a deliberately different **linear SSA-chordal** design — i.e. v1's shape, where virtuals are colored
> independently and call-result **capture movs are real**. v1 paid for this bug already
> ([CopyResolution.maxon:377-395](maxon-selfhosted/Compiler/Targets/Shared/CopyResolution.maxon#L377-L395)):
> the colorer can legitimately assign two result dests into a **SWAP** or **CHAIN**, which naive
> sequential movs cannot realize — `mov x1, x0; mov x0, x1` collapsed value+flag into one register, so a
> bounds check read the element value instead of the OOB flag and **panicked on in-bounds data** (the
> array-sort `try get(j) otherwise` miscompile). The fix is `sequentializeCallResultCapture`: a
> **parallel-copy sequencer with per-class cycle-break scratch**, never sequential movs.
>
> The **bootstrap is immune and its code is therefore NOT the model** — its `Assign(reg, value)` merely
> pins a value into a register map and emits no capture mov at all, so it has nothing to sequence.
> **Port v1's lesson here, not the bootstrap's shortcut.**

### 🚩 PHASE 1 GATE — the differential oracle

**Acceptance — and step 1 is the whole point:**
0. ✅ **DONE 2026-07-29 (slice G1).** Split `compilerExe` into the COMPILER-UNDER-TEST and the WORKER
   EXECUTABLE. ⚠⚠ See the box below. Without this, steps 1–4 all pass while testing nothing.
   **Gate: `scripts/worker-exe-split-gate.sh` — run it whenever the pool's dispatch changes.**
1. Compile the **parallel** harness with **`maxon.exe`** → `spec-runner-ref.exe`.
2. Compile the **parallel** harness with **`maxon-shv2.exe`** → `spec-runner-shv2.exe`.
3. Run **both** against `specs-shv2/`, both driving `maxon-shv2.exe` as the compiler-under-test,
   **both on an N-worker pool**.
4. **The two must produce identical results.**

If shv2 miscompiles the harness, the shv2-built harness's own verdicts are untrustworthy — so the
`maxon.exe`-built harness is the oracle that catches it. **Without step 1 this gate could pass
while silently broken.**

> ### ⚠⚠ STEP 0 — ONE `FilePath` IS DOING TWO JOBS, AND THE GATE IS WHERE THAT STOPS BEING FREE
> *(found 2026-07-29, while re-extracting the runner)*
>
> **`PersistentWorkerHandle.spawnNoWait(compilerExe, …)` spawns `compilerExe` — as the WORKER.**
> (declared [SpecWorkerPool.maxon:663](maxon-shv2/Testing/SpecWorkerPool.maxon#L663), spawned
> [:693](maxon-shv2/Testing/SpecWorkerPool.maxon#L693)). That one parameter is
> simultaneously *"the compiler this suite is testing"* and *"the executable a worker process is"*.
>
> **In-tree the two are the same file and always have been** — the harness IS the compiler binary, so
> `runSpecTest` passes `Process.executablePath()` and both readings land on it. The conflation has
> therefore never been wrong, never been tested, and is invisible to every green suite.
>
> **The gate is precisely the configuration that separates them**, and unsplit it does not fail
> loudly — **it passes**. `spec-runner-shv2.exe` would spawn `maxon-shv2.exe` as its workers; so would
> `spec-runner-ref.exe`; both parents would delegate every actual verdict to the SAME in-tree
> harness, the two result streams would agree perfectly, and the gate would certify that shv2
> compiles the harness correctly **without a single test having been run by shv2-compiled code.**
>
> ⇒ **`spawnNoWait`, `runSpecPool` and `runPersistentWorker` take TWO paths, not one.** The project's

### Future rungs — corpus-surfaced features that each need their own number

Distinct front-end / IR features the corpus surfaced that do NOT ride an existing rung; each gets a ladder
number when it is sequenced (each also has a `disabled-test:` or oracle-divergence pinning it):

- **⬜ A MODULE-LEVEL `var` AND A SELF-FIELD ALIAS AT A BY-REFERENCE POSITION SILENTLY LOSE THE CALLEE'S WRITE — AND THE ORACLE AGREES, SO IT IS A LANGUAGE GAP, NOT AN shv2 BUG.** Filed 2026-08-12 by PBR-2's reviewer, **reproduced by the coordinator on BOTH compilers**: `var g = 0` at module scope, `setTo99(g)` where the callee does `x = 99`, prints **`g=0`** on shv2 **and `g=0` on the C# bootstrap**. Same for an `export var` self-field alias. Neither is refused — both are mutable, so E3019 correctly does not fire — and neither is cell-resident, because `collectCellLocalNames` decides *local* names and `declareCellLocal` installs a cell only at a local `var`'s declaration. Each spills its VALUE into a scratch cell the callee writes and the caller never reads back. ⚠ **`specs/pass-by-reference.md` says "all parameters are passed by reference" but tests neither storage kind**, so its 28 cases are green over this. ⇒ These two storage kinds need a write-back or a cell of their own — **a rung, not a clause**. ⚠ What PBR-2 *did* own was the comment at the deciding line, which enumerated the non-cell case as *"a `let`, which `checkImmutableArgToMutatingParam` refuses with E3019"* — **an enumeration that fails OPEN**; it now carries both measurements and the oracle agreement.

- **⬜ A TRIPWIRE `recordParamReassign` DOES NOT HAVE, AND A STALE CLOSURE IS A WRONG ABI.** Filed 2026-08-12 by PBR-2's reviewer. `SignatureIndex.maxon:8547` can write after `closeByRefForwarding` has latched `byRefForwardingClosed`. **The ordering is sound today** — every fold completes inside `queryProgramSignatures`, before any body parses — **but nothing enforces it**, and a future reordering would be a silent miscompile rather than a loud stop. A one-line panic-if-already-latched, in the style of `bindParameters`' own tripwire, converts it. Deliberately NOT added at review time: an unexercised panic landed immediately before a merge gate can redden it for a reason unrelated to the defect. **Land it against a full-suite run.**

- **✅✅ PBR-2 — PASS-BY-REFERENCE, THE REBIND HALF — CLOSED 2026-08-12** (see the rung's own commits; 31/31 acceptance, ladder linear, one real superlinearity found and fixed by the optimizer). Kept below as the design record, INCLUDING its refuted first draft, because the refutation is the reusable part.

- **~~⬜~~⭐⭐ PBR-2 — PASS-BY-REFERENCE, THE REBIND HALF. Design RULED, contract written, RED baseline measured.** Filed 2026-08-12 by rung PBR-1, which built the *aliasing* half and stops exactly here.
  **Acceptance: `specs/pass-by-reference.md` (28 cases; measured RED 2026-08-12 at 6 pass / 22 fail on the PBR-1 tree) + `specs/refcount-byref-rvalue-scratch-slot.md` (2, both RED) + `discarded-results/impure-mutating-param` (`disabled-test:`, whose CANONICAL counterpart is live and expects exit 0).**
  ⭐ **DESIGN RULED: HEAP CELLS, not v1's stack slots — and the reason is not preference.** Three measured facts, and each kills an alternative:
  (1) **`closure-capture-after-mutation` is a WRONG ANSWER today, not a refusal** — `var x = 10; let f = function() gives x; x = 99; apply(f)` returns **10** where the spec says **99**, because shv2 captures BY VALUE (`Parser.maxon:53627-53632` predicted this verbatim: *"a captured-then-mutated `var` would differ, and no test exercises that"*). A closure escapes its frame, so **no** call-site write-back design can serve it. ⇒ SSA write-back is out.
  (2) **wasm has no address-of-local**, so `stackAddr` would have to box into linear memory anyway ⇒ v1's design is *heap cells plus a target-specific fast path*, not an alternative to them. A copy needs a reason and this one has none: both references use stack addresses because both have slot-based IRs and mem2reg; shv2 has neither, and already leans on heap boxes twice (the closure `__env`, and "a struct IS a heap box").
  (3) **cells satisfy the `bindParameters` tripwire BY CONSTRUCTION** (`Parser.maxon:20274-20298`). Its hazard is CALLER-side — `increment(n)` in a loop has no `=` for `assignsAt`'s lexical scan, so no phi is minted and `n` silently resets. A cell-resident binding leaves the phi-tracked class entirely, so the missing phi becomes *harmless* rather than needing the scan taught. ⇒ **do NOT flip `ParametersAreMutable`; do NOT teach `assignsAt` a call-site form.**
  ⛔⛔ **CORRECTION 2026-08-12, MEASURED BY PBR-2's IMPLEMENTER AND CONFIRMED BY THE COORDINATOR — THE PARAGRAPH BELOW IS WRONG ABOUT THE SEAM, AND IT IS KEPT ONLY SO THE ERROR IS NOT RE-MADE.** `semanticCheck` **cannot** promote a BINDING, because **a binding does not survive parsing**: `VarInfo.boundValue` is documented as *"the SSA ValueId this binding ALIASES"* (`Project.maxon:363`) and ARCHITECTURE.md:356-362 says `let x = 42; return x` mints no `x` op at all. ⇒ **`let m = n` and `n` are ONE ValueId**, so a post-parse pass cannot tell a use of `m` from a use of `n` and would redirect both — `var n = 5; let m = n; setTo99(n); print(m)` would print the post-call value. The mis-transfer was mine: `promoteArgsNeedingAWritableRecord` rewrites an **argument at a call op**, an OPERAND position, which survives parsing; a **binding** is not that kind of object. ⚠ Both references can do this late only because **names denote slots all the way down** (v1's `stackAddr` on a scope slot; the bootstrap's `StdLeaOp` plus a post-call reload keyed BY NAME at `MaxonToStandardConversion.cs:2437-2467`). shv2 has neither.
  ⇒ ✅ **RULED: IT LIVES IN THE PARSER, FED BY THE PRE-BODY SIGNATURE SWEEP** — `queryProgramSignatures` completes before any body is parsed and **already carries a whole-program, per-parameter, BODY-DERIVED fact**: `scanConsumeBits` (`Parser.maxon:11107`) + `solveAndPublishTransitiveFeeds` (`:12511`), consulted by the parser at call sites via `calleeConsumesArgument`. Seed lexically on `assignsAt`; close forwarding by a **program-wide gate** rather than a fixpoint, so there is **no second call-resolver**. ⭐ The gate is a TESTABLE PREDICTION: parameter reassignment is E2013 today, so no stdlib function can carry a seed, so **every gate-off program must emit byte-identical code** — which is exactly what the golden-drift delta measures.
  ⭐ **WHERE IT LIVES — ⛔ SUPERSEDED, see the correction above. The seam already exists and already has a precedent.** "Does callee `g` reassign parameter `k`" is a whole-program fact over BODIES, and shv2's parser is a single forward pass — but `semanticCheck` runs whole-program after all parsing/merging and **already performs exactly one non-diagnostic Maxon-IR rewrite driven by exactly this data**: `promoteArgsNeedingAWritableRecord` (`LiteralArgPromotion.maxon:81-331`, called last at `SemanticCheck.maxon:93-100`) reads `ParamMutationSummary` and splices ops around call arguments. PBR-2 is that pass shape in that seam — it rewrites a **binding's representation** where the precedent rewrites an **argument's value**. Seed a *second* mask (`reassignedParamMask`, narrower than `writtenParamMask`) and close it on the existing `collectCallParamEdges` fixpoint; v1 has the identical duality (`computeReassignedParams` for the ABI vs `computeMutatedParams` for E3019).
  ✅ **Block args survive the representation change** — `PruneDeadBlockArgs` / `ElimTrivialBlockArgs` are purely SSA def/use (*"IT NEVER REWRITES A VALUE"*), a block arg's type is only a register-class tag, and pointers ride the same integer band. A loop-invariant cell pointer is the `φ(v, phi)` shape those passes fold as trivial.
  ✅ **HALT CHECK ALREADY DONE, and it is CLEAR**: across the whole ported corpus **no live pin asserts E2013 on a PARAMETER** (every one targets a `let` local, a loop variable, a match binding or a top-level `let`), and the **32 live E3019 pins** across 7 files encode the rule PBR-2 must PRESERVE and EXTEND, never invert. ⚠ The 4 `for-iterated-self-field` E2013 pins are the **iteration lock**, an orthogonal safety mechanism, and must stay refused.
  ⚠ **The bootstrap is NOT the oracle for `refcount-byref-rvalue-scratch-slot` case 1** — see the stale-flag E3019 bug in *Bootstrap oracle bugs*.
  ⚠ **v1 is a SOURCE to read, not a design to copy**: `MaxonBorrowCheck.computeReassignedParams:147`, `LowerMaxonToStd.buildByRefParamKeys:5461` / `byRefArgAddress:10446` / `allocByRefScratchSlot:10505`, `InsertRefcounts.isByRefRvalueScratchSlot:1453` with its two sweeps (`:4685`, `:4840`). ⚠ **shv2 has NO `InsertRefcounts` Std pass at all** — it refcounts in the PARSER (`ownedBindings` / `emitScopeDrops` / `drainPendingTemps`), so v1's slot-keyed sweeps have **no analogue to port into**; that is the hardest single item and it is a DESIGN task, not a port.

- **⬜ E3070's SUBJECT IS A BASE NAME, so a borrow of one field collides with a store to a SIBLING field.** Filed 2026-08-12 by PBR-1's reviewer, coordinator-triaged as out of that rung. `b.name = "x"` (managed, non-array) under a live borrow of `b.items` over-refuses, because the borrow and the store both carry subject `b`. **Pre-existing, not created by PBR-1** — `b.other.clear()` already collides with a borrow of `b.items` the same way — so it is a PRECISION rung: subject granularity would have to become a field path rather than a base name. ⚠ PBR-1 did fix the acute half it *did* create (a **scalar** field store, which frees nothing, was refused under any live borrow rooted at the base — measured against the oracle, which compiles and runs it).

- **⬜ A BY-REFERENCE FORWARDING EDGE CANNOT READ ITS RECEIVER'S TYPE, so a user METHOD still collides with a `stdlib` method of the same name — a FALSE REJECT whose only workaround is renaming.** Filed 2026-08-12 by the `refcount-reassigned-slot-borrow` tick, which closed two thirds of this and measured the third precisely. **The measured program is `temp/methodswap`** — `type Holder` with a reassigning `swap(n Node)` — which dies on `E2015: overloading 'Array.sort'` in a program that never mentions sorting. ⭐ **THE CARRIER IS ATTRIBUTED BY SABOTAGE, NOT INFERRED**: `stdlib/helpers/sort/smallSort.maxon:32`, `Array.swap`'s own `try managed.swap(i, j: j)` — the receiver is a FIELD, so the token sweep can read neither its type nor the callee's, and the bare `swap` reaches every method wearing that name. Routing that one call's arguments through locals makes the identical program compile and exit 99. ✅ **Already closed and pinned**: a root-level FREE function sharing a stdlib method's name (a dotted call has no route to one), and a user method sharing the name of a stdlib method reached only `self.`/`Self.`-qualified (that receiver IS the enclosing type, statically — which covers every sort helper). ⚠ **DO NOT close it in `stdlib`** — rewriting `Array.swap` to dodge the widening is an accommodation in library source hiding a compiler limitation, and holds only until the next stdlib method hands a bare parameter to a dotted call. ⇒ It needs the RECEIVER'S TYPE at the declaration sweep: either a field-type roster available before bodies are scanned, or an arity/labels test on the edge. ⚠ Blast radius is a REFUSAL being lifted, so the false-reject sweep IS the rung — and note the precedent from the tick that filed this, where lifting the same refusal one shape over exposed a live wrong answer (`0x3F3F3F3F` freed-slab fill) that the refusal had been masking.

- **⬜ THE DURABLE-SLOT REBIND PROTOCOL IS PROSE AT FOUR DOORS AND CODE AT NONE — one fact, four copies, and a divergence that reads as a wrong answer at RUN TIME rather than as a compile error.** Filed 2026-08-12 by the reviewer of the `emitFieldWrite` acquire-order fix, which is exactly what this duplication cost: `Parser.emitFieldWrite` had been ordered release-then-acquire for the whole life of the door, and the three siblings that argue for the opposite order in their own headers had no way to say so. The four doors are `reassignCellBinding` (`Parser.maxon:23189`), `emitCheckedGlobalStore` (`:23435`), `emitFieldWrite` (`:52986`, fixed) and `emitOpaqueFieldReassign` (`:53096`, **still release-first and deliberately so** — see its own comment: safe only because `valueIsOwnedHeap` makes its acquire emit no IR, and a scheduled widening to a real retain would reproduce the use-after-free there). Each spells `acquire → release(load) → store` itself over its own load/store pair, and nothing makes them agree. ⇒ A `DurableSlot` union (`cell` / `global` / `field`) with ONE `emitDurableSlotRebind` would make the ordering a property of the compiler rather than of four comments; the doors differ only in the `{Load, Store}` emitter pair and in the acquire's flavour.
  ⭐ **AND WHILE CONSOLIDATING, RE-DECIDE THE ORDER — the stated reason for release-BEFORE-store has expired.** `reassignCellBinding:23164` justifies release-before-store as *"BEFORE the store overwrites the only pointer to it"*, but all four doors now load the displaced value into an SSA temp first (`:23190`, `:23437`, `:52960`, `:53096`), so the store cannot lose it. **`acquire → store → release` is therefore strictly safer at identical cost**: it closes the window in which the slot still holds a pointer to a record a generated destructor may already have destroyed. Reaching that window today needs a reference cycle (`box.f` holds `c`, `c.g` holds `box`, releasing `c` takes `box` to zero), which is why it is a rung and not a bug. ⚠ It re-mints goldens across the suite — the acquire-order fix alone moved 8 — so it needs the cross-target lanes, not `/spec-port`'s host-only battery.

- **WITNESS DISPATCH DOES NOT TYPE-CHECK ITS ACTUALS AGAINST THE REQUIREMENT'S FORMALS — the `E3005` a DIRECT call already gets.** Filed 2026-08-03 by P1.7a Slice E, which **deferred it twice and was wrong both times**, then closed the crash path so it is genuinely deferrable now. Measured: `g.greet(loud: 5)` at a `greet(loud bool)` requirement compiles in **shv2 AND in the bootstrap** (exit 7 — `5` silently read as `true`) while the direct-call twin is properly refused; `slottedWitnessArgs` checks arity and labels and never types the actuals. Both directions are open (`true` at an `Integer` formal also compiles). ⚠ **It is not merely a missing diagnostic — with the ABI now taken from the FORMALS, a mismatch is a crash or a wrong answer**, which is how it produced a backend panic (`xmm0 → rdx crosses register files`) that a control compiled correctly. `LowerMaxonToStd.maxon` says the gap out loud at the derivation site. ⇒ The check must compare against the **SUBSTITUTED** formals (associated types resolved through `associatedAbiBindingOf`) and must **reuse the direct call's checker**, not write a second type comparison. Blast radius is corpus-wide — a new refusal, so the false-reject sweep IS the rung.
- **A PARSE-TIME CONFORMANCE REGISTRY — what would let an associated-type RETURN be SUPPORTED instead of refused by E3120.** Filed 2026-08-03 by P1.7a Slice E, after a coordinator ruling to substitute the binding was **measured not implementable** and the implementer refused rather than half-fix it. `Parser.interfaceReturnMaxonType` mints the dispatch result's tag from the interface's rendered spelling **during parsing**, but `project.conformances` is filled by `ParseStaging.mergeArtifact` — after every file has parsed — and `ProgramSignatures` records interfaces, structs, enums and aliases but **no `implements` clause**, so the parser has nothing to ask. Nor can it be deferred to lowering: `TypeResolution` rewrites function SIGNATURES and explicitly never the parser's `valueTags` column, so a lowering-only fix corrects the call's ABI and still leaves `m.make() + 11` picking an integer add on an f64. ⇒ A `conformanceDeclSites` sweep plus a fold, mirroring `interfaceDeclSites`/`foldInterfaceDeclarations` and riding `ProgramSignatures.hash`. ⚠ **It touches the parse-memo key**, so every incrementality gate is in its blast radius — which is why it is a rung and not a ride-along. E3120's registry entry names this sweep as its fix.
- **A GENERIC-INSTANCE RESULT IS NOT DROPPED AT A WITNESS CALL SITE — a reachable `exit 101` leak.** Filed 2026-08-03 by P1.7a Slice E; **attribution measured, not assumed**: a `Box with Integer` or `Array with Integer` returned through a witness dispatch leaks, while the SAME instance through a **direct** call is clean (7) and a **`String`** through the SAME witness path is clean (7) — so the front end types the result correctly and this is a missing **drop**, a distinct ownership mechanism, not the front-end gap E3120 covers. Reproduces through a plain `where T is` generic with **no existential involved**, and is unchanged by the `declaredNameIsManaged` door that closed the associated-type form. ⚠ The leak gate sees it (exit 101), so it is pinnable the moment the mechanism lands.
- **WIDENING A CONCRETE CONFORMER DIRECTLY INTO AN EXISTENTIAL FIELD — refused today, and the refusal is the deliberate half of P1.7a Slice 2.** Filed 2026-08-04 by `P17a2`. `Self{t: m}` where `t` is interface-typed and `m` is a concrete conformer is a positioned **E2015** naming the workaround every spec already uses (*"pass the value to a named function taking the interface as a PARAMETER and store THAT parameter, which arrives already widened"*) — **coordinator-verified to run, and review-verified to be inescapable** (probed through a requirement returning an interface, two such requirements, and a requirement with both an existential parameter and return). ⭐ **The reason it is a rung and not a ride-along was MEASURED, not predicted**: the second word is the conformer's witness-table address, which only a widening SITE can name, and a field store has no callee whose declared parameter types could name it. The verdict needs `ConformanceCheck.valueWidensToInterface`, which takes a whole `Project` **the parser does not hold by design** — an `implements` clause is recorded when its own file parses and the two files have no ordering. The implementer BUILT the widening op and reverted it: it rippled into **8 files outside the slice** (`MaxonDialect`, `SemanticCheck`, `ConformanceCheck`, `StdlibSource`, `DeadGlobalElimination`, `ValueOrigin`, `FnRefThunk`, `StringRuntime`) plus a new whole-program check. ⇒ **the design is already worked out**: append `witnessTableAddr(result, conformerName, interfaceName)` to `MaxonOp`, lower it to `rdataAddr(ensureWitnessTable(…))`, and verify conformance by walking those ops in `ConformanceCheck` the way `dispatchedInterfaceNames` already walks `witnessDispatch`. ⚠ Until it lands, **a path reaching `ensureWitnessTable` with an unverified conformer PANICS the compiler** — that is what the refusal is holding shut.
- **`Parser.handleEscapingBorrowFeed:41633` HAS A BARE `__mm_incref` ON A VALUE CLASS THAT ADMITS `interfaceRef` — the exact shape `P17a2`'s review just fixed one door over. ⚠ LATENT, NOT LIVE.** Filed 2026-08-04. Increfing an existential whose conformer is a String literal is a read-modify-write of immortal `.rdata` — measured as **exit 139** at the door that WAS reachable, and cured there by the witness table's new retain word (`__str_clone` / `__mm_retain` / zero). This door is unreachable today because a generic instance cannot be built over an interface (`Box with Hashable` is **E2015**). ⭐ **NO SPEC CASE WAS WRITTEN, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE** — there is no program that reaches it, so a case would pin nothing; this follows `A2e`'s precedent for a latent residual. **The re-measure trigger is exact: the day an interface may be a generic type ARGUMENT, this door is live**, and the fix is already written next door — route it through `ExistentialOwnershipProtocol` instead of hardcoding `__mm_incref`.
- **A `Character` RENDERS ITS CODEPOINT UNDER INTERPOLATION — `"ab{c}"` gives `ab99`, not `abc`.** Filed 2026-08-04 by `P17a2`'s review, which tripped over it building an unrelated control and reported it rather than absorbing it. Far outside that rung's cone (nothing existential, nothing to do with ownership or the return ABI) and **unmeasured beyond the one observation** — reproduce it first, and check the bootstrap's answer before assuming which side is wrong, because `/specs` is canonical for the oracle and this is exactly the shape where the two compilers have disagreed before.
- **🔴 BOOTSTRAP ORACLE BUGS — TWO OPERATORS CRASH `maxon-sharp` ON A FLOAT-BACKED ENUM, and shv2 now answers both correctly** (found 2026-08-03 by BATCH13 and its review; the **"Bootstrap oracle bugs"** list is their home — each needs the full C# suite as its gate, and `maxon-sharp/` was held by another lane at the time). **(1)** `-Weight.light` on `enum Weight  light = 2.5` dies with **`E9001: … Unable to cast StdF64 to StdI64`** in `MaxonToStandardConversion.Run` — its front end types the value f64 and then cannot lower the negation. A plain float negates fine there, so the crash is enum-specific. shv2 now prints **-2.5**. **(2)** `Weight.light shl 1` dies with **`E9001: Unsupported binop: Shl on Float`**; shv2 refuses it cleanly with `E3005: operator 'shl' requires integer operands, but this one is float`. ⭐ **THE POLARITY IS INVERTED AGAIN, which is now the third time in this family** — `A4l` established the oracle was WRONG about float formatting, `A4o` that it was RIGHT about float-backed enum rendering, and these two that it CRASHES where shv2 answers. ⇒ **the oracle is not uniformly the reference on floats, and each question must be put to it separately.** Both pinned on the shv2 side by `specs-shv2/enums-simple.md`'s `float-backed-negation` and `error.float-backed-enum-shift`.
- **🔴 BOOTSTRAP ORACLE BUG — `-x` OVER A FLOAT VARIABLE IS `0.0 - x` IN `maxon-sharp`, SO `-(+0.0)` IS `+0.0`.** Filed 2026-08-30. `2-Parser.cs:19224-19230` emits `MaxonLiteralOp(0.0)` + `MaxonBinOp(Sub)` for every non-literal float negation — exactly the trade shv2 shipped until the same day; under the bootstrap `let z = 0.0; print("{-z}")` prints `0.0` and `Json.parse("-0")` answers `+0.0` (a literal `-0.0` is right there too, through C#'s own `-` on a `double`). **shv2 is FIXED**: a genuine `MaxonUnaryOp.fneg` / `StdUnaryOpcode.fneg`, native `fneg` on arm64 and `f64.neg` on wasm, and on x64 `TargetOp.negF64RegReg` (`xorpd` against a mask built in xmm5 — its header records why not an `.rdata` mask). Pinned by `specs-shv2/float-negative-zero.md`'s `negating-a-zero-variable` / `const-negation-of-a-float-constant` and `stdlib-whitelist.json-negative-zero-round-trips`. ⚠ No oracle golden can see this — the oracle agrees with the wrong answer — so it needs the full C# suite as its gate; the bootstrap already has an aligned `.rdata` mask mechanism (`GetOrCreateAbsMask`/`EmitAbsF64`) a `xorpd` can ride.
- **shv2 NEVER EMITS E3097, SO AN ACCESSOR COMPARISON THE ORACLE REFUSES IS SILENTLY ACCEPTED.** Found 2026-08-03 by BATCH13 while porting `specs/constants.md`. The code is registered and specced (`error.enum-accessor-comparison` — `c.ordinal == 1`) and the oracle refuses it; shv2 compiles it and answers. ⚠ **An OVER-ACCEPTANCE, so the corpus cannot catch it by running** — the ported case is `disabled-test:` naming this. It is about the accessor-comparison ban, not about enum backing, which is why it did not ride BATCH13. ⚠ Note shv2's **own source** already writes around the pattern (`Targets/Shared/RegBits.maxon:346-352`), so the rule has a live constituency.
- **A MODULE-SCOPE `let X = Enum.case` IS `E2010`, because the top-level constant initializer reads a dotted name as a RANGED-ALIAS BOUND.** Found 2026-08-03 by BATCH13 (`Expected 'min' or 'max' but got 'green'`). It is the same door three `array-globals` cases already wait on, so it closes more than one case. One ported `constants.md` case (`top-level-constant`) is `disabled-test:` on it.
- **⚖ NEEDS A RULING — shv2 REFUSES `return <enum> ` FROM A NUMBER-RETURNING FUNCTION WHILE THE ORACLE ACCEPTS IT, AND shv2 DISAGREES WITH ITSELF ACROSS TWO COERCION SITES.** Found 2026-08-03 by BATCH13's review. `return Level.high` from a `returns Whole` is `E3005: Cannot return 'Level' from function declared to return 'int'` — **for an INT-backed enum as much as a float-backed one** — while the oracle accepts it and prints the value; yet shv2's own struct-field STORE accepts the identical conversion. ⚠ **It is a REFUSAL, never a wrong answer**, and it is about enum→number *assignability* rather than about how bits are read, which is why BATCH13 did not widen into it: closing it ENLARGES the language surface and that is a decision, not a fix. ⇒ **rule first (is an enum implicitly a number?), then make the two coercion sites agree whichever way it goes.** Related, minor, and probably the same conversation: `trunc(4.0)` prints `4` on the oracle and `4.0` on shv2.

- **THE REMAINING E3012 SUBJECTS — the 8 cases `specs-shv2/unused-variables.md` still carries as `disabled-test:`.** Opened 2026-08-03 by `A4g` (BATCH12), which ported that file byte-identical and unlocked the `for` binding only. ⭐ **THE `for` BINDING WAS SEPARABLE AND THESE ARE NOT ALL SEPARABLE THE SAME WAY, WHICH IS THE WHOLE REASON THE SPLIT IS HERE RATHER THAN ARBITRARY**: `for _ in` is already legal in BOTH compilers, so the refusal had a legal escape hatch before it was written. **(a) BODY LOCALS** (`unused-var`, `unused-let`, `multiple-unused-first-reported`) are NOT separable — `Parser.maxon`'s own header records that the local rule needs **E2001** (`let _ = expr` ⇒ "use `_ = expr`") and **E3064** (pure result unused) to land WITH it, or a borrowed element that may be neither bound, nor discarded, nor used has no legal spelling at all; `underscore-discard` adds **E3067** (`_ = <non-call>`) to that same knot. ⇒ **one rung, four diagnostics, or none of them.** **(b) THREE MORE BINDING KINDS, each merely a missing candidate-mint site and individually cheap**: `tuple-destructuring-unused` (`let (a, b) = …`), `unused-match-binding` (`createPayloadBinding`), `unused-otherwise-binding` (the `otherwise (e)` handler). **(c) CLOSURE PARAMETERS** (`unused-closure-param`) is a deliberate abstention, not a gap — `parseClosureExpression` collects candidates and DISCARDS them ("NO E3012 DRAIN HERE"); the oracle checks each closure independently, so closing it means giving a closure its own drain. ⚠ **Whoever takes this inherits `A4g`'s measured trap**: "referenced" is a fact about the NAME within the function, not about the binding, and the corpus programs that depend on it are NOT ported — see `specs-shv2/unused-variable-name-scope.md`, which exists to pin exactly that.
- **🔴 BOOTSTRAP ORACLE BUG — a closure capturing a name that an intervening `for` binding shadowed is `E9001` (the "Bootstrap oracle bugs" list is its home; it needs the full C# suite as its gate).** Found 2026-08-03 by BATCH12's reviewer while probing `A4g`'s name-scoped mention set. `let i = 5` ; `for i in 0 upto 3 'a' … end 'a'` ; `let f = function() gives i + 1` ⇒ **`error E9001: … 'a_0' does not dominate 'a_0.exit'`** on `maxon-sharp`, where **shv2 compiles it and prints 6**. The oracle appears to resolve the closure's `i` to the LOOP's binding rather than to the enclosing `let` that is still in scope at the capture. ⚠ **shv2 is the one that is right here**, so this is a case where the runnable oracle cannot be consulted about closure capture across a shadowing loop — relevant to anyone taking the closure half of the E3012 entry above.

- **⬜ u32 MEMORY ACCESS — `ExitCode` IS A SIGNATURE/ABI TYPE AND NOT YET A STORAGE TYPE** (D7's tail +
  W1b, 2026-07-30, MEASURED not predicted). `parseTypeReference` claims `String` and `Character`
  syntactically and deliberately does NOT claim `ExitCode`, because that door answers for the VALUE column
  too: promoting it makes `ExitCode` a STORAGE type, `var n as ExitCode` becomes a u32 field, and
  `Targets/Shared/StdLoweringShared.maxon`'s `accessWidthFor` panics — *"no memory-access form for u32"*.
  **Measured: claiming it there was 2578/3**, all three the same panic. ⚠ **Why it is its own rung:** the
  panic is DELIBERATE and its cure is a backend slice — a narrow unsigned load/store needs the width AND
  the sign-extension form chosen per ISA, so it needs a contract across x64, arm64 and wasm, and
  `accessWidthFor` is the shared door all three come through. Same `as`-cast family P1.9 deferred (`i8 to
  i32` panics one line above for the signed twin). ⚠⚠ **AND THE SINK LIST ITSELF CHANGES THE DAY IT LANDS.**
  Today the env slot is the ONE place a narrow type reaches memory — which is why W1b's `envSlotStorageType`
  carve-out is sound and does NOT generalize; every other store takes its width from a DECLARED slot type
  (`fieldStorageType` at three sites, `payloadStorageOf` at three more) or from a fixed i64 (the GT/async arg
  spill stores every argument at i64 regardless of type). Claim `ExitCode` in `parseTypeReference` and all
  six see a narrow type for the first time — struct fields, union payloads, globals — and the env-slot
  answer must be RE-DECIDED against real 4-byte packed fields rather than copied.
- **⬜ AN OVERLOAD SET PUBLISHES ONE RETURN TYPE FOR THE WHOLE SET — `returnTypeOf` IS KEYED BY THE BARE
  NAME** (found 2026-07-30 by D10's review, measured on both compilers; a D7 × D10 interaction, and
  neither rung's own defect). D7 mangles a REGISTRATION by parameter types but `ProgramSignatures.
  returnTypeOf` still answers for the bare name, keeping the FIRST declaration's return type for the set.
  ⭐ **The leak direction is already blocked, and not by D10**: a MIXED set — some members void, some
  value-returning — is refused by D7's own guard (*"the overloads of 'Helper.f' do not agree on their
  return type"*), probed with `struct`, `String` and `int` returns alike, so no discarded box exists.
  An ALL-VOID set works end to end (both members callable as statements, measured). ⚠ **What is wrong is
  a FALSE REJECT**: in a mixed set the genuinely void member is refused in statement position with
  `E2015`, while **the oracle compiles and runs it** and shv2 itself accepts the value-returning sibling
  in expression position in the same program. ⚠ **Why it could not ride D10:** the only change available
  inside `voidStaticCallsAt` is to let a non-void `declared` fall through to the unknown-member arm — and
  that would claim `Point.create()`, discard its box, and create exactly the leak D10's negative spec
  pins. The real fix is **D7's index becoming per-MEMBER rather than per-NAME**, which is the boundary
  D7's own diagnostic text describes, and it is a distinct rung rather than a ride-along.
- **⬜ A NESTED CLOSURE THAT CALLS AN ENCLOSING CLOSURE PANICS THE COMPILER, FOR ANY TYPE** (found
  2026-07-30 by W1b's review, PRE-EXISTING and independent of both W1 and W1b). `let v = n; let f =
  function() gives v; let g = function() gives f(); return g()` ⇒ **`panic at TypeResolution.maxon:672:
  resolveTypes: 'unresolved' reached type resolution — the parser emits no unresolved placeholders at
  M1`**. Reproduced with a plain `Integer`, re-measured on `main` at W1b time, so it is nothing to do with
  `ExitCode`, widths or the env-slot door W1b fixed — a closure VALUE captured into another closure never
  gets its return type resolved. Legal source, hard crash. ⚠ **Why it could not ride W1b:** W1b's footprint
  is the env slot's WIDTH; this is `closureReturns` threading through a NESTED env, which is P1.5-A2's
  mechanism and wants its own survey of how a lifted closure's file-local return type reaches an inner
  closure's call site.
- **⬜ E3036 HAS TWO HAND-WRITTEN SENTENCES, AND THE HELPER THAT EXISTS TO PREVENT THAT SAYS SO IN ITS OWN
  HEADER.** **Filed 2026-08-02 by `/spec-port`'s review of `stdlib-autodiscovery`.** One arity fact, two
  spellings, nothing making them agree: `Project.argArityMismatchMessage` (`:2721`) renders *"'{callee}'
  expects {expected} argument(s) but {got} were provided"*, and `Queries.maxon:991`'s `builtinArity` arm
  hardcodes *"'{name}' takes exactly {expected} argument, but {got} were given"* — same
  `ErrorCode.callArgCountMismatch`, different words, different grammar. The helper's header argues the
  principle explicitly (*"Two mechanisms, one rule — so the text lives here rather than at either site"*),
  which is what makes the third raiser bypassing it a drift rather than a choice.
  ⚠ **No spec will ever surface this**, so the port whitelist will never reach it: BOTH spellings are
  pinned green — the helper's by six live cases (`functions.md`, `method-calls.md`, `where-clauses.md` ×2,
  `first-class-functions.md`, `implicit-self-methods.md`, `parsable-interface.md`), the hardcoded one by
  `builtins-clock.md` and `builtins-sleep.md`. That is precisely why it needs a row rather than a queue
  position.
  ⚠ **It needs a RULING before a fix**: unifying moves two already-ported specs' expectations, which is
  out of bounds for a port tick (`/spec-port` HALT). Decide which sentence wins, then re-mint the two
  goldens with it.
- **⬜⬜ A `bool` COMPUTED FROM A FLOAT COMPARISON AND HELD ACROSS A LOOP READS BACK FALSE — A SILENT
  WRONG ANSWER ON PLAIN USER CODE.** **Found 2026-08-02 by `/spec-port` while listing `stdlib/Math.maxon`;
  PRE-EXISTING and nothing to do with that entry.** ⭐ **Reproduced minimally, with an oracle control —
  21 lines, no `Math`, no stdlib, no generics:**

  ```maxon
  typealias Real = float(f64.min to f64.max)

  function probe(x Real) returns ExitCode
      var val = x
      let isNeg = val < 0.0            // TRUE for x = -8.0
      if isNeg 'neg'                   // ... and this arm IS taken
          val = -val
      end 'neg'
      var n = 0
      while val > 1.0 'reduce'         // a loop whose compare writes EFLAGS
          val = val / 2.0
          n = n + 1
      end 'reduce'
      if isNeg 'wasNeg'                // ... but THIS one is not
          return 11
      end 'wasNeg'
      return 22
  end 'probe'

  function main() returns ExitCode
      return probe(-8.0)
  end 'main'
  ```

  **MEASURED: the C# bootstrap returns 11, shv2 returns 22.** The first `if isNeg` takes its arm and the
  second does not, in one function, with no assignment to `isNeg` between them.
  ⚠ **AND IT IS ALREADY LIVE IN THE STDLIB, not only in a probe: `stdlib/Math.exp` is this exact shape**
  (`is_negative = val < 0.0`, held across `while val > 1.0`, re-tested at `invert`). **MEASURED
  independently at review, 2026-08-02: `Math.exp(-2.0)` is `< 1.0` under the bootstrap and `>= 1.0` under
  shv2** — the reciprocal is silently skipped, so every negative argument gets a wrong number.
  `sin`/`cos`/`log`/`log2`/`atan` carry the same hold-a-flag-across-a-loop shape and want checking with it.
  The spec case that listed the module is `Math.exp(0.0)`, which takes the early return and cannot see it.
  ⭐ **THE MECHANISM IS SHOWN OUTRIGHT BY THE GOLDEN, not inferred** — verified independently by the
  reviewer and by the coordinator before this entry was written. At `@Math.exp` the FIRST
  `if is_negative` (`ifcont:`) emits its own `x64.ucomisdRegReg xmm1, xmm0` immediately before
  `x64.jcc above, neg`. The SECOND (`forexit:`) emits **NO COMPARE AT ALL** — a bare `x64.jcc above,
  invert` whose EFLAGS come from the preceding block `forhdr:`'s `x64.cmpRegReg rcx, rax`, the squaring
  loop's INTEGER counter compare. At loop exit `rcx == rax` ⇒ ZF=1 ⇒ `above` is false ⇒ the reciprocal is
  skipped, which is exactly the measured `Math.exp(-2.0) >= 1.0`. So the `bool` is materialized nowhere and
  the second test consumes a clobbered condition code. **What remains INFERRED is only the GENERALITY** —
  which producers/consumers of a comparison-derived `bool` take this path, and therefore how wide the fix
  and its sabotage must be. The float compare is very likely incidental (the clobber here is an *integer*
  `cmp`), but that is the survey the rung owes.
  ⚠ **Why it is its own rung and could not ride the port that found it:** the fix is backend flags
  liveness, so it needs a decision at `Targets/Shared` and an equivalent one on **arm64** (cross-target
  consistency is binding), plus sabotage to prove the guard is load-bearing. **And it wants a spec of its
  own** — the corpus has ~3,420 cases and not one of them catches this, which is the more alarming half of
  the finding.
  ⚠⚠ **A COMMITTED GOLDEN NOW PINS THE MISCOMPILED LOWERING** —
  `specs-shv2/fragments/x64-windows/stdlib-basic/stdlib-call-exp.test`, minted by the tick that found this.
  A golden records what the compiler emits, so it is a correct artifact of a wrong compiler; **re-mint it
  with `--update-required` as part of this rung and do not read it as a specification.**
- **⬜ THE UNUSED-BINDING CHECK (E3012) DOES NOT EXIST IN shv2 AT ALL** — not for parameters, not for
  locals. **Found 2026-08-02 by `/spec-port` on `specs/unused-parameters.md`, 4 of whose 6 cases it
  blocks.** ⚠ That tick DEFERRED the spec, and deferring was abolished the same day (user ruling;
  `.claude/skills/spec-port/SKILL.md` §4). `unused-parameters` is back in the loop's whitelist order and
  **this row is the work its next tick has to do**, not a reason the spec waits. Measured, not
  inferred: `docs/error-codes.txt` E3012 carries `csharp` and `selfhosted` claims and **no `shv2` line**,
  and shv2's sources contain no emitter under any spelling (grep for both the member name and the message
  text — the check is structural, since `ErrorCode.<name>` does not compile unless the registry generated
  it). ⭐ **The backlog for it already exists and is bigger than the one spec**: `unused-variables.md`
  (whitelist 170) and `var-should-be-let.md` (175) are unported and sit on the same mechanism, and **four
  cases across three ALREADY-PORTED specs are shelved waiting on it** —
  `discarded-results/underscore-not-prefix-suppression`,
  `interface-conformance/non-interface-method-on-conforming-type-still-errors`,
  `interface-conformance/interface-method-local-var-still-errors`, and
  `ternary-expression/…unused-loopvar-before-ternary`. ⚠ **Why it is a rung and not a port tick, and it is
  not the use-count that makes it one — it is the four rules layered on top, three of which are already
  written down as contracts:** (1) an **interface-method exemption** — the implementer is forced to declare
  every parameter the contract names, and `interface-conformance`'s two shelved cases exist precisely to
  pin that the exemption does NOT extend to non-interface methods on the same conforming type, nor to
  locals inside an interface method; (2) the **`_` discard rule** — `_` binds nothing and is exempt, while
  `_x` is an ordinary variable that is not (`discarded-results`); (3) **two precedence orderings the
  registry states outright** — E2028 `matchTypeMismatch` is thrown at parse time *"so it wins over the
  body-finish unused-variable check (E3012)"*, and E3012 in turn beats **E3077** `SemanticVarShouldBeLet`
  (*"an unused `var` reports as unused, not as should-be-let"*), which shv2 does not claim either, so the
  two want sequencing together; (4) a **whole-program false-positive surface** — this is a check that goes
  from silent to loud across every function in `stdlib/` and all ~3,390 corpus cases at once, which is the
  blast radius no rapid-iteration tick can carry and the reason the spec was deferred rather than
  part-landed.

- ~~**⬜ THE SPEC RUNNER WEDGES NONDETERMINISTICALLY**~~ ⭐ **SEQUENCED as board row `H1` (2026-07-30) — take it there, not here.** ⚠ And the signature recorded below is CORRECTED on the row: the PARENT was at 1.7–1.9% CPU, not 0% — only the workers were idle — which is what identifies the dispatch loop's poll fallthrough as the thing spinning and re-points the suspicion at the parent→worker handshake. Original filing follows:
- **⬜ (superseded by H1) ALL WORKERS IDLE AT 0% CPU, INDEFINITELY.** Hit **TWICE
  in one session** by the T1 coordinator (2026-07-30), on the arm64-macos host: once on the host lane, once on
  the wasm lane, in a tree whose identical binary then ran the same suite **green in 5.5 s and 8.1 s** after a
  `SIGTERM` and a retry. Signature both times: the parent plus all **12** workers in `STAT=S` at **0.0% CPU**
  for **10+ minutes**, zero output written (the runner buffers, so an empty log is expected and is NOT the
  tell — the CPU column is), and on the wasm lane **no `wasmtime` process ever spawned**. ⚠ **Not a target
  issue and not T1's** — T1 touches no runner code, and the wedge struck both lanes. `pkill -TERM` cleared it
  with **zero** processes left behind, so the old *"kill wedges the box"* hazard is genuinely gone. ⚠⚠ **This
  is the single biggest threat to running rungs UNATTENDED**: a wedged gate is indistinguishable from a slow
  one until you look at `%CPU`, and a `/loop` that simply waits will sit on it forever. Suspect the same
  family as the GT scheduler race fixed 2026-07-20 (`8163f1056`) — a residual, or a second one.
  ⇒ **Diagnostic that costs nothing: `ps -o pid,etime,%cpu,stat -p $(pgrep -f 'maxon-shv2 spec-test')` — all
  workers at 0.0 for minutes means WEDGED, retry rather than wait.**

  while `synthesizeFnRefThunk` builds `sig.paramCount() + 1` = 2. ⇒ an ABI/arity change across
  `LowerMaxonToStd`, `FnRefThunk` and the wasm functype interning — three files W1 does not touch — needing
  its own acceptance cases for higher-order function values. The existing guard's own comment already names

- **✅⭐⭐ TUPLES (first-class, HEAP-ALLOCATED) — CLOSED 2026-07-29** (main `f25737501` · `867126aca` · `e6ccf3d5e` · `25f9aefd3` · `2921a6468`; x64-windows **2372 → 2401/0**, x64-linux PASS, wasm PASS, build 0 warnings, **arm64 SKIP — remote, UNVERIFIED**). `Map` and `for (k, v)` remain OPEN and are the follow-on rung (below).
  ⭐⭐ **A TUPLE IS A SYNTHESIZED STRUCT, NOT A TYPE-SYSTEM ARM.** `(10, 32)` mints a `StructLayout` under a mangled name (`__Tuple2.int.int`) and the value is typed with the existing `MaxonType.structRef(TypeNameId)`. **Measured cost of the alternative: ~25 exhaustive `match` sites** across `TypeRules`/`MaxonDialect`/`LowerMaxonToStd`/`LayoutDescriptor`/`Parser`/`SignatureIndex`/`SemanticCheck`/`TypeResolution`/`TypeNameInterner` would each have needed a new arm. Taking the synthesized-struct route, `TypeResolution.maxon`, `LowerMaxonToStd.maxon` and `MmRuntime.maxon` needed **no edit at all**, and destructors for a tuple containing a `String` came free from the existing `installStructDestructors` walk over `project.structTypes`.
  ⭐ **THE SLICE BOUNDARY WAS MEASURED, NOT JUDGED.** Only **2 of the 18** canonical cases assert allocation (an `mm-trace` block): `small-tuple-return-allocates-nothing` and `for-in-over-map-allocates-no-tuple`. **Every other case asserts an exit code, which heap-allocated tuples satisfy** — which is exactly how v1 ships them. So the two-register ABI is worth **one test**, against a new calling convention on x64 + arm64 + wasm; it is its own rung. 15 of 18 unlocked here.
  ⛔⛔ **THE TWO REFERENCES SPLIT, AND THAT DECIDED THE DESIGN.** On STRUCTURE they agree almost line for line (comma disambiguator after the first inner expression; positional `_N` fields; `.N` → `_N`; destructure via a hidden temp; `for (k,v)` special-cased). On the **ABI they do not**: the bootstrap implements the register pair (verified in its own IR — `RAX`+`R10`, no `mm_alloc`, `R10` chosen because a throwing call already uses `RDX`), while **v1 has no such thing at all** — every tuple heap-allocated, `ret` takes one value, no escape analysis. Corroborated: `stdlib/Map.maxon:359`'s `current() returns Entry` would necessarily allocate per iterator step under v1, which is the exact allocation the spec's own MmTrace case says does not happen. ⇒ `specs/tuples.md`'s ABI section targets the BOOTSTRAP, not v1.
  ⭐ **A DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM BOTH REFERENCES, RULED BY THE COORDINATOR:** `t.0.1` (chained tuple access) lexed as `identifier`, `dot`, `floatLiteral(0.1)` because `scanNumber` greedily eats a following `.` as a fraction. **Both references REJECT it** (oracle: `E2010 Expected identifier but got '0.1'`; v1 makes it a parse error). shv2 now **accepts** it. Justification: the corpus is **silent** — no case, no doc mention — so nothing in the definition is contradicted; both references fail it *incidentally* via a greedy float scan rather than by design; and accepting more never invalidates a valid program. The rule is exact (a digit can follow `.` for exactly one reason — there is no `.5` form). Pinned by an shv2-only case that says so.
  ⭐ **THE MANGLED-NAME JOIN IS `.`, NOT THE BOOTSTRAP's `_`, FOR INJECTIVITY.** `_` is inside the identifier alphabet, so `(A_B, C)` and `(A, B_C)` both spell `__Tuple_A_B_C` — one layout, two element lists, and the second silently *becomes* the first. This is the project's own lossy-key-used-as-identity shape. Sabotage-verified.
  ⭐ **TUPLES ARE COPIED WHERE A STRUCT IS MOVED**, at two sites gated by one predicate, restricted to trivial-element tuples (a managed element keeps the struct rules — stricter, never wrong). **Oracle-verified**: `xs.push(p)` then reading `p` back returns 7 there too.
  🔴 **THE REVIEW FOUND TWO BLOCKERS, BOTH FROM ONE ROOT CAUSE** — a tuple type had **two `MaxonType` spellings** reaching the generic-instance registry, which keys on `(tag, id)` while the mangler reads only the name: (1) a spurious **`E3006`** rejecting a valid program, blaming a `typealias` written once; (2) a **compiler PANIC**, `resolveCallFixups: call to unknown function '__destruct___Tuple2.Num.String'`. Both attributed to the tuple commit by rebuild, both fixed, both sabotage-verified and spec-cased.
  ⚠ **THE LADDER COULD NOT SEE THIS RUNG — NINTH CONSECUTIVE, and this time trivially so:** the feature did not exist until the commit, so the corpus could not contain it. Measured rather than assumed — `--emit-corpus` wrote 465 files / 279,453 lines and every tuple-syntax grep returned **zero**. `Testing/ladders/gentuples.sh` is the committed instrument (7 modes in 4 CONTROL PAIRS, which is what lets a product term separate). ⭐ **What it found was NOT tuples**: `internArrayLiteralAggregateInstances` ran once per FILE over every type registered so far — **O(files × types)**, `phase:signatures` ×2.16→×3.03 per doubling, fixed to ×1.92→×1.99 (CPU 786M → 188M at n=1024). **The struct-only control bends identically**, which is how it was attributed as pre-existing; tuples merely added a second producer of registered types. Rung's own footprint: **+12 allocations flat**, 29 fragment additions, **zero modifications**.

- **⬜⭐⭐ `Map` + `for (k, v)` DESTRUCTURING — the follow-on to tuples, now unblocked.** The tuple half closed 2026-07-29 (above), which was the stated blocker. `Map` is compiled stdlib in BOTH references (`stdlib/Map.maxon`, open-addressed, 4 parallel `Array` fields, 75% load, tombstones — structurally shv2's `Set` plus a `values` buffer and a second drop slot). Corpus: `specs/map.md` 34 · `specs/map-struct-bytearray.md` 3 · `specs/map-try-otherwise-block.md` 4 · `specs/with-iterator.md` 6, all unported, plus `specs-shv2/tuples.md`'s 2 held cases (`for-destructuring-map`, `for-in-over-map-allocates-no-tuple`) and the 2 live `block-scoping.md` markers. ⚠ **`for (k, v)` belongs HERE, not with tuples** — measured: **zero** tuple cases use it, and shv2 has no map-like iterable to pair it with, so it had no source to iterate. ⚠ The first-class `Range` VALUE + iterator protocol (5-6 `ranges.md` cases) still rides this rung — `withIterator()` yields `(Iterator, Element)` tuples.

- **⬜⭐ THE TWO-REGISTER VALUE-TUPLE ABI — the other follow-on to tuples.** Worth exactly ONE canonical case (`small-tuple-return-allocates-nothing`, the only non-Map case in `specs/tuples.md` asserting allocation), and it is a genuinely large piece: **shv2 has no multi-register or hidden-pointer return path on any target** — one GPR (`R8`/x0), every aggregate a heap pointer, one register per argument. So this is a new calling convention on **x64 + arm64 + wasm**, plus escape analysis and a throws exclusion. ⭐ **The bootstrap is the sole model and its gate is the interesting part**: an explicit `IsGprScalar` **whitelist** (integer/bool/cstring only) means a tuple containing a `String` never enters the register path at all, so there is no "register-pair return with a dangling destructor" case to solve — the gate prevents it by construction. Throwing and address-taken functions are excluded module-wide (`R10` vs `RDX` would collide with the error flag). v1 implements none of this.

  closing it puts a whole-program query under a per-file one. That is the design question this rung owes.

- **✅⭐⭐ A RANGED ALIAS BINDS EVERY POSITION A VALUE MEETS IT — CLOSED 2026-07-29** (main `349002a56` · `57f931f60` · `0f5048d1d` · `07309764a` · `a7f3263ad` · `2ba120280` + integration; x64-windows **2337 → 2372/0**, x64-linux **2274/0**, wasm PASS, build 0 warnings, **arm64 SKIP — remote, UNVERIFIED**).
  **THE FILING WAS RIGHT AND I ALMOST CONCLUDED IT WAS WRONG, BECAUSE MY ORACLE WAS STALE.** `bin/maxon.exe` had not been rebuilt against `maxon-sharp/`; against it shv2 and the bootstrap looked BYTE-IDENTICAL on every probe — same output, same panic, same stack trace. A 54-second rebuild reversed every reading. ⇒ **STEP 1's "ALWAYS BUILD" INCLUDES THE ORACLE. It is a binary too.**
  **MEASURED DIVERGENCE:** shv2 missed the compile-time `E3005` at FIVE positions the bootstrap rejects — call argument, array `push`, struct-literal field, field default, field store — and the RUNTIME guard at a field store. `return` and `as` were already right.
  ⭐ **THE CORPUS SETTLED THE SCOPE, SO NO RULING WAS NEEDED**: `specs/range-check-panic.md` states normatively that the runtime half is emitted at a return, struct-literal field, field store, array-literal element and `as`, and **explicitly NOT at a call argument** (a documented, filed bootstrap limitation). So shv2 matching the oracle there is CORRECT, and only the compile-time half was owed — which is also why shv2 never met the arg-pinning blocker that stopped the bootstrap: no branch, no block split, no pinning pass to break.
  ⛔⛔ **NEITHER REFERENCE WAS THE DESIGN — BOTH HAVE THIS BUG.** The pre-fix bootstrap drove checks off a `MaxonValueKind`; **v1 drives them off `CastCategory`, a five-value enum with NO range field**, and checks NEITHER half at a call argument, struct-literal field, field store or local assignment. **shv2's architecture was already the right one** — a site recorded at PARSE time off the still-`named` `MaxonType`, consumed by a Std-tier pass, immune to the erasure both references died on. The rung pointed it at four more doors.
  ⭐ **THE ERASURE IS ASYMMETRIC AND THAT DECIDED THE WORK**: `resolveTypes` overwrites function PARAMETER types with bare primitives, but **struct field types are never rewritten**, so the field doors already held the alias name. Only the call argument was hard, and the RETURN had already solved it — parameter alias names are now captured in `parseFunction` exactly as `rangeCheckReturnAlias` always was.
  🔴 **THE RUNG FOUND AND FIXED FOUR DEFECTS BEYOND ITS BRIEF, EACH A WRONG ANSWER:**
  1. **Guards chained BACKWARDS.** A guard splits its block, so resolving every site to the parser-recorded block id put guard k+1's cascade *before* guard k's branch. Guards ran in REVERSE SOURCE ORDER (the compiler blamed the second of two bad casts), and `where-clauses.two-constraints` proves it was a genuine MISCOMPILE — two cascades comparing `rbx` against 0 and `r12` against 1000, mixing two fields across two checks. It also broke compare fusion, leaving N−1 `setcc` values in registers until the file overflowed at **N=16** and the RULE 3 backstop panicked. Fixed; both doors now clean at **N=512**.
  2. **A range-check site written inside a CLOSURE was filed against the ENCLOSING function** — a closure has its own SSA numbering, so ids crossed a boundary. A CORRECT program was killed at run time, and the dual let an out-of-range closure cast through unchecked. **Reachable through the `as` door before this rung.**
  3. **The guard fired at END OF BLOCK**, so the rest of the block ran first: an out-of-range value was PRINTED and read back out of a `Percent` slot before its panic, and `100 / d` panicked *"integer divide by zero"* where the oracle panics *"Range check failed"* — the language's own check pre-empted. **USER RULING: fix in-rung.** Fixed with a two-tier position (`maxonOpPos` parser-stamped, `stdOpPos` translated by one `RangeSiteWalk`), composed with the chain via `guardChainBase`.
  4. **A FALSE `E5001`** exposed by (3): `peakOutranks` resolved a full-pool tie to the highest-indexed block, so the driver relieved a chain back-to-front and refused a program that fits in two registers. Fixed by letting a value already in a slot be re-relieved at a COLD peak; loop `E5001` untouched by construction.
  ⚠ **THE LADDER COULD NOT SEE THIS RUNG — EIGHTH CONSECUTIVE, AND A NEW MECHANISM.** The manifest check PASSES (the corpus really does declare narrow aliases) but they are only ever GENERIC TYPE ARGUMENTS, erased to opaque `T` before any door sees them: **128 narrow aliases, ZERO doors**. Measured: the rung-0 and rung-5 binaries each contain exactly ONE range-check panic blob. ⇒ **A NARROW ALIAS IN THE CORPUS IS NOT A NARROW ALIAS AT A DOOR**; a manifest check must count DOORS. `Testing/ladders/genrangesites.sh` is the committed instrument that does, and it found a real `O(sites × blocks)` scan (−27.4% CPU) that the allocation column was structurally blind to.
  ⚠ **AND THE MERGE ITSELF FOUND A THIRD THING**: `origin/main` advanced mid-rung with P1.9's declaration-site half, and on the rebased tree upstream's new **E3062 pre-empted this rung's E3005** in a cross-file case whose caller-side alias was, correctly, unused. The case predated the rule and was rewritten to use it — and now proves strictly more. **Step 11's "re-run the suites if main advanced" is what caught it.**
