- **✅⭐⭐ E3070 BORROW-LIVENESS — COMPLETE 2026-07-28** (main `bb390d834` · `aef7a3480` · `2dd8dbf2b` · `03bf57153` · `d79a0ac71` · `f49f3c088`; x64-windows **1922→2003/0**, x64-linux PASS, wasm32-wasi PASS, build 0 warnings, fragments additions-only and byte-identical after a full run, no 101. ⚠ **arm64-macos/arm64-linux SKIPPED — UNVERIFIED**, owed to the hand sync). **A DIRECT PORT WAS IMPOSSIBLE, AND THAT IS THE RUNG'S THESIS:** both references key a borrow on a VAR SLOT recovered from `varDecl`/`varLoad`/`varStore`, and shv2 has none — `let` binds a name to an SSA `ValueId` in `Scope` at parse time and mints no op, so an IR pass cannot see the bindings *because the bindings are not in the IR*. So the **PARSER RECORDS** onto `IrFunction.borrowFacts` and **ONE RESOLVER DECIDES** in `semanticCheck` (`Compiler/BorrowCheck.maxon`), the first point holding the whole-program `ParamMutationSummary`. It is P1.8 Slice A's write doors asking a SECOND question of the same binding — the lock asks *"is this being iterated?"*, the borrow set asks *"is an element of it still referenced?"* — both answered from ONE derivation (`iterationSubjectNameAt`, shared via `borrowSubjectNameAt`). Three things came out BETTER than the references: liveness is **exact** (a use is a `Scope` resolution) rather than a highest-op-index stand-in; `pop`/`remove` are excluded **structurally** by `emitArrayElementAccessor`'s `owned` flag, so v1's `mutatingMethodNames` list is not ported; and nothing is recorded until a function actually borrows, where the bootstrap allocates a key list on EVERY op. **USER RULING (2026-07-28): the `for`-in element ENROLS**, so `for it in b.items 'scan' wipe(b.items) … end` is E3070 — a deliberate divergence from the oracle, which accepts it because it RETAINS. Its liveness is **LEXICAL over the loop body**, not the loop variable's last use: ordinary NLL would expire the borrow at the last use of `it` and wave through a mutation the *iteration itself* still dies on. ⭐ **EVERY STAGE OF THE PROCESS FOUND A REACHABLE DEFECT THE ONE BEFORE IT HAD CALLED DONE** — the implementer's own probing found 4 (try/otherwise, ternary and `match … gives` merges each DROPPING the borrow, and a blanket attach that falsely rejected `let n = sizeOf(try arr.get(0)…)`), cured by keying `PendingBorrow` on the accessor's **ValueId**; the OPTIMIZER found two quadratics (see the trend log); the coordinator's probe found **`b.wipe()`** — a method clearing its own field — reading freed memory (`4557430888798830399` where the oracle prints 44), which the USER ruled must be FIXED not filed, and whose cure was **ONE MASK ANSWERING TWO QUESTIONS**: `writtenParamMask` ("does passing an immutable binding here make it an error?", which shv2 answers NO for a self-field write, pinned by `self-keyword.md:self-with-params` returning 42) split from `storageWrittenParamMask` ("does this body write the storage this parameter points at?"). **NEITHER MASK CONTAINS THE OTHER — they diverge in four places in BOTH directions**, enumerated exhaustively on `IrFunction` because "a superset" is the plausible and FALSE summary. And the INDEPENDENT REVIEW found the biggest one: **E3070 could not see MODULE STORAGE at all** (the subject was gated on `self.scope.contains`, and a top-level `var` has no `VarInfo` there) — four spellings, four use-after-frees, one of which the oracle refuses with this very diagnostic, so shv2 was giving a WRONG ANSWER against its own oracle. ⭐ **Ports `specs/borrow-checker.md` and flips all 3 of `array-realloc-dangling-ref.md`'s cases — that file is now BYTE-IDENTICAL to `/specs`.** `borrow-not-live-in-otherwise` stays disabled naming **`Map` (Phase 2)**, not E3070. **DECISIONS, not residuals (none holds the rung open):** an opaque-`T` element mints no borrow (a shared generic body cannot know whether the instantiation's element owns heap; refusing would reject what the monomorphizing oracle accepts — and the reviewer probed it as *not demonstrably reachable*); a sibling field shares its base's subject (forced by soundness — `b = other` drops what `b.items` points at — and pinned by `sibling-field-shares-the-subject`); a WITNESS DISPATCH cannot be asked at all, because the conflict is keyed by callee and dictionary-passing has none, exactly as E3019 already documents for the same door; and `borrowSubjectIdOf`'s O(K²) is measured debt in Workstream O. **The superseded filing follows, kept for the reasoning:** Filed by P1.8 Slice A, whose BORROW ruling puts every `for` loop on this path. **shv2 reads a freed element and returns `0x3F3F3F3F` where the oracle either REFUSES the program or gets it RIGHT** — measured both ways by the coordinator: (a) `let it = try arr.get(0) otherwise …` then `arr.clear()` then `it.value` ⇒ shv2 **0x3F3F3F3F**, oracle **rejects, `E3070: cannot mutate 'arr' via 'clear' while it is borrowed by 'it'`**; (b) `for it in b.items 'scan' wipe(b.items) … end` ⇒ shv2 **0x3F3F3F3F**, oracle **accepts and returns the correct 5**, because it RETAINS. ⭐ **NEITHER PROGRAM NEEDS A LOOP TO REACH THE HOLE** — (a) has no `for` in it at all — so this is **pre-existing and P1.8 Slice A neither created nor widened it**; Slice A's lock closes the direct in-loop mutation route (E3019) and the two indirect routes (a field chain handed to a mutating callee; a method clearing its own field) are structurally beyond what any lock keyed on a binding NAME can see. ⚠ **The two references disagree and that disagreement IS the design question**: the bootstrap is safe here *because* it retains, v1 borrows, and **a borrow model is only sound with a liveness pass**. The cure is one of incref-on-get / copy-on-get / a real `E3070` NLL borrow-liveness pass; the code `E3070` is already RESERVED for it and the 3 `disabled-test: E3070` cases in `array-realloc-dangling-ref.md` already pin it. **Sequenced AHEAD of P1.8 slices B/C/D by user ruling, because every later slice adds borrow surface onto an unsound base.** ⚠ Do not confuse this with the ✅ retain-escaping rung, which fixed a borrow OUTLIVING its referent; this is the MUTATE-WHILE-BORROWED half, which that rung explicitly did not build.

- **✅⭐⭐ `break` INSIDE A `match` ARM TARGETS THE MATCH — CLOSED 2026-07-29** (main `46cdeae35` · `77872eee3` · `b1a733167` · `980613d66` · `015c7b939`; x64-windows **2318 → 2337/0**, x64-linux **2245/0**, wasm32-wasi PASS, build 0 warnings, scale linear, **arm64 SKIP — remote, UNVERIFIED**). Filed by P1.8 Slice A under a user ruling that it get its own rung. **ONE ROOT CAUSE, FIVE SYMPTOMS** — shv2's break-target stack held only loops, so a `match` was not a break target at all: `break` in an arm with no loop ⇒ E2047 (oracle 0) · `break 'm'` naming the match ⇒ E2047 (oracle 0) · `break 'loop'` naming the enclosing loop ACROSS a match ⇒ **E2048 "targets its own loop"**, a false reject of the only legal spelling (oracle 3) · `break 'check'` naming the match's own label inside a loop ⇒ E2047 (oracle 23) · and the filed one, an unlabelled `break` in a match in a `while` ⇒ **11 where the oracle returns 23, a SILENT WRONG ANSWER**. ⚠ **The filing named only the last two of the five**; the other three were found by coordinator probing before the wave, which is the whole reason step 2 reproduces before it plans.
  **THE RULE, and it needed no design ruling because all three authorities already agreed** — `specs/match-statements.md`'s own `## Break` documentation section states it verbatim, `docs/WRITING_MAXON_CODE.md:529-532` agrees, and both reference compilers implement it identically: **break targets = matches ∪ loops; continue targets = loops ONLY.** Unlabelled → innermost break target. `break L` naming a MATCH → always legal, any depth, **never E2048**. `break L` naming a LOOP → E2048 iff that loop is the innermost loop AND no match is open. Match EXPRESSIONS are not break targets. ⭐ The asymmetry is real and load-bearing: `continue 'loop'` written across a match is STILL E2048-redundant while `break 'loop'` across the same match is REQUIRED — measured on both compilers, and both spellings are now committed controls.
  **TAKEN from both references: TWO STACKS** (`self.matches` beside `self.loops`), not one kind-tagged stack — and the reason is shv2-specific rather than "it works there": `bindingIndexEscapesLoop` reads top-of-`self.loops` and MEANS "innermost loop", so a merged stack would silently corrupt it, whereas a second stack leaves every existing reader correct by construction.
  ⛔ **NEITHER REFERENCE'S LOWERING TRANSFERS, and that is the rung's one real design finding.** The bootstrap emits `br <label-string>` for a merge block that does not exist yet — it can, because it branches by NAME. v1 instead creates the merge block EAGERLY in `parseMatchHeader`. **shv2 can do neither**: it branches by `BlockId` (the rewrite's thesis), and `finalizeMatchMerge` mints `matchcont` **LAST, deliberately**, so it lays out after every arm body — copying v1 would move block layout and churn goldens wholesale. ⇒ **The shv2-native answer is that a match-targeted break ENROLS ITS BLOCK AS A REACHING ARM EXIT**, draining into the join path `finalizeMatchMerge` already runs. No new block, no early block, no layout change, and ONE join path instead of two.
  ⭐ **This also cured, by construction, a bug v1 had to fix twice.** v1's all-arms-break match wrongly sealed its live merge dead (`maxon-selfhosted/Compiler/Parser.maxon:9713-9729`) and needed a dedicated `mergeReached` flag, because its break blocks were detached-and-dead and invisible to the fall-through count. shv2 needs no flag: the enrolled block is left UNTERMINATED and the dead block is a fresh one that is never enrolled. Verified by the review, and locked by `match-break.every-arm-breaks`.
  **DELIVERABLE: 7 markers flipped + 12 new cases (2318 → 2337).** ⭐ **TWO of the seven were STALE MARKERS blaming the wrong mechanism** — `match-simple/match-arm-field-assignment` blamed "enum scrutinee (Wave B)" and `match-statements.break-only-arms-with-panic-arm` blamed "payload union + panic (Wave B)"; both failed purely on break-in-match, found by flipping every case that USES `break` in an arm and reading the split. ⛔ **And one of those two could NOT be unlocked** — see the parameter-field-store rung below; it is re-disabled with a measured reason, not a guess.
  ⭐⭐ **THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE IS THE GOLDENS, not the suite count: the rung moves ZERO pre-existing fragments on x64-windows AND on x64-linux.** 19 additions per target plus exactly ONE modification, and that one's diff is **the source line alone** (`break` → `break 'loop'`) with **byte-identical IR on both targets**. A change that re-targets a control-flow keyword and moves no existing byte of codegen is the strongest available statement that the new target is reached only by programs that ask for it.
  ⚠ **A COMMITTED SPEC HAD ENCODED THE BUG.** `specs-shv2/match-owned-value-flow.md: temp-scrutinee-break-arm` (an `specs-shv2`-only case, no canonical counterpart) expected exit 7, reachable ONLY if the unlabelled break exits the loop; under correct semantics nothing in its body can change `result` and the program is an **infinite loop** (confirmed: exit 124 under timeout). Repaired to `break 'loop'`, which restores exactly the loop-floor-drop property its own prose states. ⚠ **The bootstrap is not an oracle for it either way** — it refuses the program outright with `E3012 unused variable: 'n'`, a lint shv2 lacks.
  ⭐ **FOUR DECISIONS THE IMPLEMENTATION MAKES WERE UNTESTABLE FROM THE SUITE**, found by the independent review and now committed, two of them **proved load-bearing by SABOTAGE**: reversing the matches-before-loops search order failed exactly ONE test of 229 (nothing else distinguished the two loops), and dropping the `isBreak` gate on `matchDepth` turned an unlabelled `continue` in a `for` into a **compiler panic** — the existing control caught only the labelled route.
  **THE E2049 COUPLING IS NOW RECORDED IN THE CODE.** "Prefer the match unconditionally" computes "innermost break target" only because a match arm body is a single statement that may not open a loop; both references depend on this and **neither writes it down**. A push-depth counter would remove the dependency and was deliberately NOT built — speculative generality for a nesting the language forbids — so the comment names what must be re-read if E2049 is ever relaxed. The review tried every route to a loop inside an open match (`if`, `try` block forms, closures, nesting through the scrutinee) and found none.

- **✅✅ A FIELD STORE THROUGH A STRUCT **PARAMETER** IS E2013, WHERE THE ORACLE COMPILES AND RUNS IT — CLOSED 2026-08-12 by rung PBR-1** (detail row below). The permission split landed exactly as this row
  specified: the ruling's "borrow's pointee is writable, binding is not rebindable" is now two ranks
  sharing one predicate, and `p = other` on a parameter is **still E2013** — verified by the coordinator,
  because relaxing the rebind without the by-reference mechanism would compile a write the caller can
  never observe. ⚠ **The row's closing sentence — *"A FALSE REJECT, never a wrong answer, which is the
  only reason it did not have to be fixed in-rung"* — turned out to be the expensive half.** Lifting the
  refusal made a real **use-after-free** reachable (a live borrow of `b.items.get(0)` across a
  `b.items = <fresh>`), because `parseFieldAssignment` owed E3070 both doors that `emitCheckedSelfFieldStore`
  had carried all along and had nothing to guard while a parameter's box was unreachable. **A refusal can
  be masking a defect on the route it refuses**, so "false reject, never a wrong answer" is a statement
  about today's diagnostics, never about the mechanism underneath. Kept below as the closed record.
  Found 2026-07-29 by the break-in-match rung, as the SECOND and independent blocker on
  `match-simple/match-arm-field-assignment` (that case is re-disabled naming this, not break-in-match,
  which it now clears). Measured on both compilers, **all four cells**, because the obvious control is
  the wrong one: `function scan(state State)` then `state.flag = true` is **E2013 "cannot assign to
  immutable variable"** in shv2 and **compiles and runs** in the bootstrap — while `let s = State.make()`
  then `s.flag = true` is **E2013 in BOTH**. ⇒ **shv2 is RIGHT about `let` and wrong about parameters**,
  so the fix is emphatically NOT "permit a field store through any immutable binding". ⭐ It is the
  P1.4 ruling not carried through: **params BORROW by default** (user, 2026-07-18), and a borrow's
  POINTEE fields are writable even though the binding itself is not rebindable — shv2 conflates
  "cannot rebind the reference" with "cannot write through it". Reproduced with no `match` anywhere,
  so it is entirely independent of the match machinery. ⚠ **A FALSE REJECT, never a wrong answer** —
  which is the only reason it did not have to be fixed in-rung.

- **⬜ shv2 HAS NO E3071 AT ALL — UNREACHABLE CODE AFTER AN ALL-TERMINATING MATCH IS ACCEPTED SILENTLY.**
  Found 2026-07-29 by the break-in-match rung's independent review, and **coordinator-confirmed on the
  merged tree with no `break` anywhere**: a match whose every arm `return`s, followed by a further
  statement, is `E3071 unreachable code after exhaustive match or branching where all paths
  return/throw` in the bootstrap and compiles clean in shv2 (returning the right answer; the dead
  statement is simply kept). It surfaced here only because "every arm breaks to the outer loop" is a
  NEW way to write an all-terminating match, but the defect is general to the construct and predates
  this rung. A missing LINT, so the divergence is "shv2 accepts more" and never a miscompile — same
  class as the unused-`for`-variable E3012 gap filed against P1.8 Slice A. ⚠ **Not spec-portable as a
  passing case**: the oracle REFUSES the program, so the case can only be a `maxoncstderr` one, which
  is exactly what the rung that adds the lint should write.

- **⬜⭐ A GENERIC INSTANCE'S IDENTITY SHOULD BE ITS ELEMENT'S RESOLVED WIDTH, NOT THE ELEMENT'S NAME — USER RULING 2026-07-27: "match the references".** Filed by the P1.7-finish rung. **shv2 is the only one of the three compilers that can NAME a type it cannot resolve.** `SignatureIndex.ByteElementTypeName = b"Byte"` is the name a `b"…"` literal interns its `Array with Byte` under, and shv2 reads no stdlib, so nothing defines `Byte` — which is why `Bytes.create()` + `.append(b"CD")` only agrees on a stride once the *user* declares `typealias Byte = int(0 to u8.max)`.
  ⭐ **THE REFERENCE EVIDENCE, gathered before the ruling and the reason for it:** **neither reference treats `Byte` as a builtin.** The bootstrap registers it as an ordinary `IrRangedPrimitiveType` and `ResolveTypeParamName` (`2-Parser.cs:18347-18356`) resolves it to base `i8`, with `:18320-18322` **explicitly unifying `u8`/`i8` element names** so the auto-generated `__Array_i8` a literal mints and stdlib's `ByteArray` are **the same instance**. v1 does the same through `computeOptimalIntType` (`TypeResolution.maxon:4434`). **Identity is by resolved width; neither needs `Byte` defined, because neither identifies an array instance by its element's NAME.**
  ⇒ **Registering `Byte` as compiler-owned would be a DIVERGENCE from both references, not an alignment** — which is why the coordinator's first framing of the choice was wrong and the user asked for the reference answer before ruling. ⚠ This is a change to **generic-instance identity**, which P1.6-C made deliberately nominal — so it is a rung with its own contract, not a slice. It also subsumes the two divergences the finish rung's own review left open: `[1, 2 as Index]` **and** `[2 as Index, 1]` are *both* accepted by the oracle (→2) and both E2015 in shv2 (the divergence is symmetric — the implementer reported only half), and `takes([10, 20])` against an `Array with Index` parameter is E3005. ⚠ **Collapsing the literal's inference to `integer` is NOT the fix** — measured: it regresses `takes([x, y])`, which works today. The real shape is a **literal-vs-typed-value distinction** in `requireArrayLiteralElementMatches` (a bare int literal coerces into the fixed element type if in range; a typed value keeps its type), which is the same machinery **P1.8's map literals** will want.
- **⬜ A USER `type Array` / `type Set` DECLARATION IS SILENTLY INERT — USER RULING 2026-07-27: leave it, decide when real code forces it.** Filed by the P1.7-finish rung's review. After that rung nothing miscompiles (every door either routes to the builtin or reports E2015 — this was the silent-miscompile fix), but the declaration itself is accepted and does nothing, with no diagnostic saying so. ⚠ **A "builtin base name is reserved" error is NOT obviously right**, because it would fight the stdlib-whitelist roadmap: `stdlib/Array.maxon`'s own declaration is literally `type Array uses Element`, so the compiler would refuse the stdlib it intends to grow into. ⇒ **decide when the whitelist actually reaches `Array.maxon` and real code forces the answer**, rather than guessing now.
- **⬜ THE PARSE CAN BE THE FIRST WRITER OF A GENERIC INSTANCE, AND TWO WRITTEN-DOWN INVARIANTS SAY IT MUST NOT BE.** Filed by the P1.7-finish Slice-3 implementer, which **stopped and reported rather than take a policy decision inside a rung about three front-end divergences** — the right call. `arrayLiteralInstanceFor`'s `named` arm reaches `arrayInstanceForNamedElement`, which **interns**; the declaration sweep over-interns `Array with <declared struct/union>` only — **not ranged typealiases, not per-instance aliases** — so `[x]` with an `Index`-typed `x` interns `Array with Index` *during parse*, mutating the memoized `ProgramSignatures`. That contradicts `internBuiltinIntegerInstance`'s *"the sweep's call is the WRITE and every parser call is a pure READ"* and `deriveInstanceNames`' *"it warms the instances the SWEEP interned, which is exactly the set a parse can name"* — the latter existing precisely to stop a per-file fan-out writing one shared memo. **Pre-existing** (`let x = 10 as Index` then `[x]` does it today) and **not observable through the CLI** (each `build` gets a fresh `Project`, and `verify-warm-rebuild` passes) — it bites the **LSP / long-lived project** path and the future **parallel frontend**, as a cached parse artifact holding a gid a fresh index need not reproduce. Closing it means widening both the sweep's over-intern **trigger** and its **set** (structs + unions + ranged aliases + inner/per-instance aliases — a cross product), across `Parser.maxon`, `SignatureIndex.maxon` and `Project.maxon`, with its own cost curve and gid-ordering risk. **A policy decision about how much the sweep should over-intern.**
- **⬜ SUB-BYTE BIT-PACKING (`bool` + narrow ranged ints) — the boundary P1.7-finish Slice 2 deliberately did NOT cross.** Slice 2 stopped at **byte-granular** 1/2/4/8, exactly where `ComputeOptimalIntType` stops. v1 goes further, packing any zero-based `upper <= 15` into **1/2/4 BITS** (`BuildLayoutDescriptors.maxon:406-462 packedElementBits`), and both references bit-pack `bool`. That needs a **negative `element_size` encoding** and has its own unported corpus: `specs/bool-bit-packing.md` (20 cases) and `specs/ranged-int-bit-packing.md` (11), neither in `specs-shv2`. ⚠ Also still 8: an **enum**-element array, which hits the machine-word fallback for a *different* reason (an enum is not a ranged int) and was left alone deliberately.
- **⬜ SIGNED NARROW ARRAY STORAGE.** P1.7-finish Slice 2 narrows on the **unsigned** ladder only — a negative lower bound keeps 8 — because `ArrayRuntime.emitLoadElem` is one shared byte loop that **zero-extends**, with no signedness anywhere in the record. **Measured**: narrowed naively, an `int(-5 to 5)` storing `-5` reads back **251**. Both references narrow signed because they carry a static signed element type into the load (the bootstrap monomorphizes; v1 stamps `StoreWidth` + signedness). Needs a runtime/ABI channel for signedness — a rung, not a widening.
- **⬜ `sizeof(<ranged alias>)` DIVERGES FROM THE ORACLE.** shv2 answers **8**; the bootstrap answers **1** for `Byte`, **4** for `int(0 to 100000)`, in both a generic body and at a concrete site. shv2 is *internally consistent* (verified by the Slice-2 review), so this is a divergence rather than a wrong answer. Closing it means teaching `Parser.concreteSizeofBytes` to see an alias's bounds — it sizes an already-**resolved** type today — and narrowing `typeLogicalByteSize` in lockstep. ⚠ **That is exactly the desync the Slice-2 implementer measured and correctly declined to half-do** (`Sizer with Byte` read `sizeof(T)`=1 off the descriptor while `sizeof(Byte)` folded to 8 in the same program).
- **⬜ THE `__ManagedMemory` BUILTIN — the `arr.managed` door.** `stdlib/Array.maxon:106` really does declare `export var managed as ElementMemory`, so `.managed` is a genuine language feature. ⚠⚠ **THIS ROW'S PREMISE AND ITS NUMBERS ARE BOTH STALE — MEASURED BY `ARR0` 2026-08-10, AND IT DID NOT CLOSE THE ROW.** The record is still synthesized (`Runtime/ArrayRuntime.maxon` IS the `__ManagedMemory` floor) but the file is no longer skipped — `stdlib/Array.maxon` is LISTED — and **the door WORKS**: `a.managed.length()` resolves, R4.4 serves a 19-member surface (`length`/`capacity`/`get`/`set`/`setLength`/`setByte`/`byteAt`/`elementSize`/`grow`/`toCString`/`makeCharFromBytes`/`append`/`slice`/`clear`/`remove`/`swap`/`shiftRight`/`shiftLeft`/`createCursor`), `specs/managed-memory-builtin.md` **IS** ported, and `managed-memory-methods.md` is down to **9** disabled cases rather than 12. ⇒ what is left of this row is those 9; someone should re-read them and either close it or restate the gap in today's terms.
- **⬜ A WIDENING BYTE-STRING BLOB.** Would turn Slice 2's review-added E2015 (a `b"…"` literal in a program whose `Byte` is wider than one byte) into working code, by emitting the blob element-wise at the declared stride. **Same mechanism a widening `__arr_append` across differing strides needs** — the two should land together.
- **⬜ `specs/lexer-parser-robustness.md` IS 0% PORTED**, and it contains `truncated-after-open-bracket`, directly on P1.7-finish Slice 3's mechanism. shv2 answers `E2004 3:1 "Expected expression but got 'end of file'"` where the oracle answers `E2007 3:11 "Unexpected end of input, expected expression"` — different code *and* column, and **shv2 does claim E2007** (`parserUnexpectedEof`), it just does not use it here.
- **◑ THE SPLITTER'S POSITIONAL STRUCTURE — LARGELY PAID 2026-07-27 (merged `e40405890`), AND STILL OPEN.**
  **Allocations went QUADRATIC → LINEAR (×3.96 → ×1.98 per doubling); CPU went N^1.83 → N^1.25 (×3.57 → ×2.48).**
  At `genwidelive` N=400: allocations 2,019,538 → **25,905** (−98.7%), CPU 6,243M → **1,670M** (−72.7%).
  ⭐ **On the many-function scale corpus `regalloc:splitting` is now LINEAR IN BOTH COLUMNS** (allocations ×1.96,
  CPU ×2.12) — the residual N^1.25 is specific to ONE function carrying Θ(N) simultaneously-live values.
  Gates: suite 1794/0; 243 goldens byte-identical; `valuesSplit` 96/196/396 unchanged; x64-windows / x64-linux /
  wasm32-wasi / arm64-macos all PASS; **arm64-linux SKIP** (see the cross-target gate defects below).

  **⚠ THREE THINGS THIS ENTRY USED TO SAY WERE WRONG, and each cost design time:**
  1. **"a lazy range-add / range-max over op positions"** — the per-INTERVAL form is the obvious shape and the wrong
     one. A split cuts one value's range over a stretch Θ(function) wide, so it needs interval endpoints in every block
     of that range **including the pass-through blocks**, re-derived from live sets that are mid-edit. What shipped is
     a **per-op MAX-SUFFIX-SUM**: the backward sweep is a running population `L(p) = L(p+1) + e(p)`, so a block's peak
     is a max-suffix-sum of ONE PER-OP number, and `e(p)` separates per value —
     `contrib(w,p) = (w is a USE operand of p) − (w is live AFTER p)` — so a split's repair is
     **O(uses of one value), never O(blocks in its range)**.
  2. **"the pool is static per op, including the REDUCED pool at fixed-register points"** — there is NO reduced pool at
     a fixed-register point. `classPoolSizeOf(pool, class, file)` is a pure function of three FUNCTION-level constants.
     What a call imposes is `forbidden[v]`, a PER-VALUE mask feeding Hall's condition (`allowedRegistersOf`). So the
     full-pool test is a range-max against ONE constant per class and needs no per-op offset.
  3. **"it needs order maintenance (an implicit treap or equivalent)"** — overstated. **Gap-labelled SLOTS** suffice
     (`SlotGap = 4`), which is what shv2 already does BETWEEN blocks via `SeqStride`. (`SplitEdits.resequence`'s binary
     search is NOT the alternative: it repairs coordinates of records that already exist and says nothing about where a
     NEW op goes, which is the whole question a splice asks.)

  **⚠ AND THE PRESCRIPTION WAS INCOMPLETE — the tree ALONE does not move the exponent.** Measured: 2a alone read
  ×2.81/×3.14, barely moved; 2a+2b read ×2.25/×2.45. Only ONE of the four walks was a range problem. The other three
  were **"walk the whole block to service an O(1) value set"** — `sweepBlockPressure` rebuilt `forbidden` for just the
  victim + its fresh ids, and `reindexSplitValues` re-indexed the same handful. Those are **EDIT-PROPORTIONAL**
  problems (walk the values' USE LISTS), not range-structural ones.

  ⭐ **`chooseVictim` — this entry's own prediction was RIGHT, and the coordinator wrongly overruled it.** Profiled
  BEFORE the fix it was **below 2%** and was struck off as disproved; with the terms burying it removed it is **7.0%**.
  A term measured small behind a dominant one is not a term disproved.

  **⛔⛔ THE CONFINED HALF IS STILL QUADRATIC, AND THIS RUNG DID NOT FIX IT — MEASURED 2026-07-27, and it
  CORRECTS THIS ENTRY'S OWN FIRST CLAIM.** The entry originally said `confinedPeakAt`/`hallVerdictAt` was
  "49.5% of the splitter and LINEAR (×2.03/×2.07), so debt not defect". **That reading was corpus blindness of
  the known kind, on BOTH standing ladders at once**, and it is the reason to state a shape before a verdict:
  - `genwidelive` is one big block but has Θ(N) values against a 14-register pool, so it sits in **FULL-POOL
    mode for ~386 of its 396 splits** — Hall barely engages, and reads linear.
  - the scale corpus IS in confined mode from its first analysis, but its **blocks are small**, so the
    O(block) confined walk is tiny and also reads linear.
  **The product of the two axes — a LARGE block in CONFINED mode — is what neither expresses**, and
  `gen12i.sh <N> 8` reaches it exactly: at `intsPer ≤ 10` **100% of splits are confined**
  (`valuesSplit` == `forced at fixed-reg points`, measured 159/159, 319/319, 639/639 at N=32/64/128).
  On that shape, at head: allocations **69,537 → 269,494 → 1,062,605 = ×3.88 then ×3.94**, CPU ×4.11 then ×4.42.
  **That is QUADRATIC in the exact column.** A/B against `d28583442` proves it **PRE-EXISTING, not introduced**:
  base reads ×3.98 / ×4.14 on the same inputs. **What the rung bought here is the CONSTANT — allocations
  −85.7% / −86.0%, CPU ≈ −14% — and NOT the exponent.**
  **⇒ MECHANISM, and it is one line of code:** `resweepBlock` calls
  `analyzeBlockPressure(wantFullPool: false, wantConfined: wantConfined)`. 2a moved the FULL-POOL peak onto the
  positional index (O(log ops)); **the CONFINED peak still requires the per-op backward walk**, so once a
  function enters confined mode the pass reverts to its pre-rung Θ(splits × block) shape. Profiled at N=64:
  `analyzeBlockPressure` **81.4%**, `confinedPeakAt` 59.0%, `hallVerdictAt` 56.2%, `augmentValue` 38.3% —
  while `refreshAfterSplit` is only 11.1%, i.e. **2b's edit-proportional work is holding; this is the confined
  re-sweep alone.**
  **⇒ WHY THE 2a TRICK DOES NOT TRANSFER DIRECTLY, and where it still might.** Hall feasibility is a property
  of a SET, not a number: there is no per-op aggregate with an associative combine (knowing [a,b] and [b,c] are
  feasible says nothing about [a,c], and adjacent ops have different live sets), and even ONE point cannot be
  maintained cheaply because adding a value triggers an augmenting path that may rewire arbitrarily many prior
  assignments. **A matching is a flow problem, not an aggregation problem.**

  **⛔ TWO DESIGNS FOR THIS ARE NOW REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT (2026-07-27). Do not re-derive either.**

  **(D1) "Index the census SCREEN and run the matching only at candidates" — CANNOT RANK, so it buys nothing.**
  `RegPoolCensus.screenViolates` is a count and IS range-additive, so it can find CANDIDATES. But a confined
  rank's `pressure` is `tight`, and `tight = countConfinedTo(allowed, witness)` where
  `witness = tightRegisterSet(...)` is alternating-path reachability over the FINISHED maximum matching
  (`HallCondition.maxon:567-568`), with a consistency panic at `:575-578` that makes the dependency
  STRUCTURAL. `screenViolates` returns a bare `bool` and stops at the first violating `p` (`:379-384`).
  Since `peakOutranks` orders confined ranks PRIMARILY by `pressure`, an index of the screen can identify
  candidates but never ORDER them — and the screen fires at ~44% of ops, so you still run the matching
  Θ(block) times per split.

  **(D2) "MEMOIZE the per-op verdict and invalidate proportionally to the edit" — DEAD TWICE OVER, both
  measured on `gen12i.sh <N> 8`, N=32/64/128.**
  - **The obvious invalidation rule is Θ(block).** *"Ops whose live set changed, plus ops where a value whose
    `forbidden` mask changed is live"* sums **×3.98 then ×4.00**; mean per split 233 → 463 → 923 (×1.99), max
    per split 2,224 → 4,528 → 9,136. **Cause: an unbroken RELOAD CASCADE.** `let s = scaleSeed()` is live
    across the whole function; one reload serves all its after-peak uses, so the fresh id is live across every
    remaining call and is itself the next victim — N/2 times, each over a Θ(N−i) range. **19% of splits carry
    89.7% of the width.** `markRunStarts` exists to break exactly this, but its rule is *"the op leaves this
    file NO register at all"* and **on x64 no op clobbers all 14 GPRs** (`SplitLiveRanges.maxon:4475-4495`), so
    the INT cascade is unbroken by design.
  - ⭐ **A LINEAR invalidation set DOES exist — and it still does not save the design.** Invalidating where the
    MULTISET `{allowedRegistersOf(v) : v live at p}` changed (which is all `hallVerdictAt` reads) sums
    **×2.01, ×2.01**, mean 29.5/29.5/29.6, **max per split 46/46/46 — FLAT across a doubling ladder**, because
    a victim and its reload have IDENTICAL allowed sets so almost every op cancels.
  - ⛔ **The killer is REACHING the invalidated ops, not finding them.** Recomputing a verdict needs the live
    set AT that op, and shv2's only route is `fillLiveBeforeOp` (`SplitLiveRanges.maxon:3348-3377`), a backward
    walk seeded from the block's live-OUT. That reach cost is **×3.94 then ×3.97** — mean per split
    651 → 1,278 → 2,533 — **quadratic INDEPENDENTLY of the cascade**, and it is ~45% of today's whole sweep.
    ⇒ ***The memo's MISSES are not the cost. REACHING them is.*** Any design that must materialize a live set
    at an arbitrary op inherits this, and that is the sentence to re-read before proposing the next one.

  ⭐ **(R2) THE ROUTE THAT REMAINS, and it is a COUNT after all — but of the right quantity.** Hall is
  infeasible at `p` iff `∃U : #{v live at p : A(v) ⊆ U} > |U|`. A minimal violating `U` is always a **UNION OF
  THE LIVE VALUES' OWN ALLOWED MASKS** — if `U` violates then so does `U' = ⋃{A(v) : A(v) ⊆ U}`, which is no
  larger — so enumerating the union-closure of the distinct masks is **EXACT, not a screen**. For each candidate
  witness `U`, `tight_U(p)` is a per-value-INTERVAL count: precisely the range-additive shape
  `PressureIndex.leafDelta` already carries per class, repairable in O(uses of one value) by the same
  `applyValueToPressure` machinery. **The confined peak becomes an argmax over `(slot, U)` read off the tree —
  no live set, no matching, no memo, so it escapes the `reach` trap.**
  **The number that decides it is the witness-family size, MEASURED:** distinct `allowedRegistersOf` masks are
  **2** on `gen12i` at N=32/64/128 (**flat in N**) and **8** on `genwidelive 100 sum`.
  ⚠ Two real risks, both needing red-before-green: (a) whether the union-CLOSURE stays small on the committed
  corpus, not just on ladders; (b) **the tie-break is a GOLDENS question** — the counting formulation picks the
  MAXIMAL violating `U` while today's code reports the Dulmage–Mendelsohn canonical one, and `peakOutranks`
  compares `(pressure, atFixedRegisterOp)` derived from it.
  ⚠ **OPEN, and do not assume it:** the memo argument above needs `tightRegisterSet`'s witness to be independent
  of WHICH maximum matching `augmentValue` happens to build (D-M canonicity). **The panic at
  `HallCondition.maxon:575-578` does NOT prove it** — that identity holds for any maximum matching. Probe it
  before building on it.
  📌 **The measuring scaffold was deliberately NOT committed** (a compile-time `let MeasureInvalidationWidth`
  plus interval/symmetric-difference width helpers, ~110 lines in `SplitLiveRanges.maxon`): it is O(function)
  per split and must never ship enabled. Its shape is recorded here so it can be rebuilt.

  ### ⛔ DO NOT BUILD R2 YET — THE EXPOSURE WAS MEASURED, AND NOTHING REAL COMES NEAR THE SHAPE (2026-07-27)

  Before designing the fix I asked the cheaper question: **does any real workload put the allocator into
  confined mode with a LARGE block?** The quadratic needs BOTH factors large *in the same function*
  (Θ(N) confined splits over a Θ(N) block). **They never co-occur outside a ladder built to make them.**
  Predictor = `confinedSplits × maxBlockOps`:

  | corpus | largest product | that row's block | its confined splits |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `gen12i 64 8` (synthetic, known-bad) | **920,315** | 2,885 | 319 |
  | spec suite, ORDINARY specs | **5,193** | 577 | 9 |
  | spec suite incl. deliberate regalloc stress specs | 44,880 | 5,610 | **8** |
  | scale corpus rung5 | 87,040 | **85** | 1,024 |
  | `genwidelive 200 sum` (known full-pool) | 11,280 | 1,410 | 8 |

  - **Ordinary real code is 177× below the synthetic shape.** In aggregate the confined half walks
    **330,146 ops across ALL 1,840 spec programs put together**; ONE `gen12i 64 8` compile walks
    **823,072** — a single synthetic file is **2.5× the entire real corpus**.
  - **802 of 803 confined-splitting functions take FEWER THAN 16 confined splits** (max 19, in a 217-op block).
  - **The scale corpus's 87,040 is not a near-miss**: its block is CONSTANT at 85 ops across all six rungs
    while the split count doubles — total confined-walk ops 8,564 → … → 255,634, ratios 1.93 … **2.00**.
    Only ONE factor grows, so it is exactly linear and always was.
  - **`x64-large-frame-arg7` has the block and not the mode**: 5,610 ops, 796 splits, **8 confined**. The
    size is there; the confined half is not. That is `genwidelive`'s shape pinned as a spec.
  - **Mechanism, and it looks structural:** confined mode is entered by almost everything that splits
    (803 of 826) — what is rare is a large block, and what does not occur is a large block that ALSO splits
    many times while confined. Reaching it needs N call sites in one straight-line block *each* carrying its
    own cross-call live set. Real large blocks (interpolation chains, byte-literal detach, `__gt_subp_spawn`)
    are large because of SEQUENTIAL work, so their live sets stay small and their split counts stay single-digit.
  - Secondary, for whenever R2 is revisited: distinct `allowedRegistersOf` masks in real code are **2–6, mode 2**.
    `gen12i` = 2 and `genwidelive` = 8, so **the ladders BRACKET the real range rather than sitting inside it.**

  ⇒ **VERDICT: the fix is speculative and has NO TRIGGER TODAY.** ⭐ **The trigger, now nameable instead of the
  vague "pressure growing" that let this go unmeasured twice: a GENERATED or MACRO-EXPANDED straight-line
  block with many call sites, or SELF-HOST (P2) — the compiler's own long straight-line dispatch functions are
  the first plausible candidate, and cannot be measured until shv2 compiles itself.**
  ⚠ **Two corpus facts this probe corrected, both of which had been assumed:**
  **(1) shv2 does NOT compile `stdlib/*.maxon` through its own register allocator at all** — every
  stdlib-shaped name reaching the splitter is a SYNTHESIZED runtime function (`__arr_*`, `__destruct_*`,
  `__gt_*`, `__mm_*`, `__set_*`, `__str_*`), so stdlib exposure is fully contained in the spec run.
  **(2) THERE IS NO THIRD REAL-CODE CORPUS — none of the checked-in examples compile under shv2**
  (verified: `examples/fannkuch-redux.maxon` E2015 `for` statement; `examples/nbody.maxon` E3009 float→int
  narrowing; `bench/sortbench.maxon` E2015 `String.toByteArray`). **Self-host is not the only gap**, and any
  future claim about "real Maxon code" has exactly the spec suite behind it and nothing else.
  📌 The exposure probe was also NOT committed (a compile-time `let ProbeConfinedExposure` + one walk counter

  **Ladder + knob are the deliverable here: `Testing/ladders/gen12i.sh <N> 8 <out>`, doubling N.**

  by the splitter positional-structure rung, which they cost ~95 minutes.** `scripts/cross-target-gate.sh` /
  `scripts/remote-mac.sh`. The gate's own contract is *"Unreachable ⇒ SKIP, and the gate still passes… but a SKIP is
  reported, never folded into the green."* Both defects break it.
  **(1) `orb run` HAS NO TIMEOUT.** The arm64-linux preflight is `orb run -m maxon-linux true` — a trivial `true`
  inside the OrbStack guest. With a WEDGED guest it blocks **forever**: measured **82 minutes at 0.0% CPU**, while
  `orb list` cheerfully reported `maxon-linux  running`. A capped re-probe never returned inside 60 s either, so the
  block is uninterruptible. **A gate that hangs is strictly worse than one that fails** — it produces no verdict at all.
  **(2) ITS FALLBACK MESSAGE THEN BLAMES THE WRONG THING.** After the hung run was killed, the script reported
  *"INCOMPLETE — the Mac went away mid-run (ssh exit 255)… Most likely it went to sleep."* **The Mac never went away** —
  it answered `ssh` throughout, and the 255 came from the kill. A wrong diagnosis in a gate is worse than none: the
  next reader retries at a different time of day instead of looking at the VM.
  **(3) A PREFLIGHT FOR ONE LANE TAKES DOWN A DIFFERENT LANE.** `arm64-macos` is NATIVE and needs no OrbStack at all,

  prints `git apply --stat` and the command, so it is safe to run against a clean tree.
  ⇒ Fix wants: a timeout on every remote probe, per-lane preflight isolation, and a fallback message that reports what
  was actually observed rather than guessing.

  Filed 2026-07-26 by the P1.7 disjointness rung's independent review, which went looking for whether the newly
  reserved instance names could collide with a witness label and found **the same defect one namespace over, needing
  no generic-instance name to reach it.** `__witness_<conformer>_<interface>` joined with a bare `_`, and `_` is a
  legal type-name character, so `(conformer A_B, interface C)` and `(conformer A, interface B_C)` both labelled
  `__witness_A_B_C`. **Coordinator-reproduced:** two interfaces, two conformers, two `where T is …` holders, right
  answer **43** — shv2 built **exit 0, no diagnostic, and returned 33**, and the same program with the underscores
  renamed away returned 43. ⭐ **The RENAME-CONTROL is what proved it**, because the bootstrap is not an oracle here:
  measured, it refuses the colliding program **and the underscore-free control identically** (`E4006`), so its
  refusal is a general constrained-type-param gap, orthogonal to the collision.

  *"idempotent by label"*, so the second pair never contested the first: **it silently BECAME it**, taking the first
  pair's table and never recording its own relocations. Which pair won is **dispatch order, not declaration order**
  (isolated by the review: same declarations, reversed dispatch ⇒ 33 vs 44).
  **The fix — the single mint site now joins with `.`** (`IrInterface.witnessTableLabel`), injective **by character
  class**: the lexer admits only `[A-Za-z0-9_]` inside an identifier, so the join has exactly one split and
  injectivity is a property of the LEXER, not of a decoder. (Escape-by-doubling would NOT have worked — with a
  one-byte separator a run of five underscores admits three valid splits.) With the label injective its memo key IS
  the pair, so no second pair-keyed memo was added. ⭐ **The argument is shv2's own:** `ensureWitnessTable` already
  called `qualifiedMethodName` — which joins with `.` — to name each witness slot's reloc target, so a table's
  *contents* were injectively named while the table's own *label* was not, **in the same function. One namespace,
  two separators, one of them lossy.**
  ⚠ **NEITHER REFERENCE IS A SOURCE HERE, AND BOTH DEMONSTRATE THE PRINCIPLE ELSEWHERE.** The bootstrap has **no
  witness tables at all** (it rewrites interface call sites statically), yet picks `.` for its one dispatch-critical
  join *because `.` is illegal in an identifier*; v1 has the **identical bug at four duplicated sites**
  (`BuildWitnessTables.maxon:86,189,245` + a hand-rolled recompute in `LowerMaxonToStd.maxon:14627`) and documents
  the collision class for its sibling `__layout_*` label, yet applies the illegal-separator rule to
  `"{qualifiedName}~static"` with the reason spelled out. **We took the principle, not the code.**
  🔴 **THE REVIEW'S FIND — THE INJECTIVITY PROOF NAMED THE HALF THAT CANNOT PROMISE IT.** The comment claimed *"a `.`
  cannot occur in EITHER half"*. False: `mangleTypeArg`'s `named` arm returns interned type names, which include the
  qualified per-instance spellings `joinQualifiedName` builds (`IntWrapper.Idx`) — so what keeps a dotted conformer
  out today is a **front-end gate, not the lexer the comment credited**. The fix survives because injectivity needs
  only **one** half separator-free, and the interface half is a single `identifier` token, so the split at the LAST
  separator is exact whatever the conformer holds. The guard now sits on the half that carries the promise
  (`requireSeparatorFreeLabelComponent`, `IR/Maxon/IrInterface.maxon:168` — reading the byte **out of** the separator
  constant so it cannot drift; R10 generalized it from `requireSeparatorFreeInterfaceName` because
  `witnessSlotImplKey` needs the same scan for a second component), proved
  live by sabotage. *Same defect class the previous rung's review caught twice: a safety argument naming the wrong
  mechanism.*
  ⭐ **DUPLICATION ADJUDICATED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT ARGUMENT.** `WitnessLabelSeparator` and `Parser.MethodNameSeparator`
  hold the same byte and are used in the same function — the project's signature shape. Verdict: **two facts**, and
  the evidence is that their admissible sets differ (the method separator is pinned to exactly `.` as surface syntax
  both references emit; the label separator admits any of ~30 bytes outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]`). Moving the witness
  separator alone to `#` produced **60 golden mismatches and ZERO wrong answers** — one fact written twice would have
  produced a wrong answer.

  `rdataOffsetOf`/`dataSectionOffsetOf` **panic by name** on a missing one — one map, two opposite opinions about how
  far it could be trusted. A re-registration whose **bytes differ** now panics. ⚠ **It would NOT have caught this
  bug and the header says so**: two equal-method-count witness tables carry byte-identical zero-filled blobs, so only
  the label could separate them. Kept because it is a **panic, not a user diagnostic**, and it catches the residue the
  separator does not — the `__layout_` shape. Hit count **measured at zero** by sabotage (full suite + 256 tables +
  4096 sites + the ladder).
  **Optimizer: no compiler change, and the reason is measured.** The scale ladder's Δ0 is a **corpus blind spot** —
  `ScaleCorpus.maxon:554` generates no `where` clause, so `ensureWitnessTable` is never called — so the rung was
  measured on a purpose-built witness ladder instead: **+0 allocations, +0 bytes** across 256→4096 dispatch sites and
  16→256 pairs, linear on both axes (the label is minted per *site*, before the memo check). It also ran down the
  log's `+612`, reproduced it on the *base* binary, and traced it to a filename-path-length term in the byte column
  plus a bootstrap refresh — **no number was "fixed"**; the allocation column is immune and reads 0.
  **Goldens:** 56 `x64-windows` fragments moved, every one of the 190 changed lines exactly `__witness_X_Y` →
  `__witness_X.Y`, verified mechanically; `x64-linux`/`arm64-linux`/`arm64-macos` **empty** (witness tables need the
  x64-only `funcAbs64InRdata` reloc). 5 new cases in `specs-shv2/type-name-collision.md` — the P1.7 disjointness

- **✅ STACK ARGUMENTS — >6 PARAMETERS — CLOSED.** The six-parameter cap is GONE, not raised: it was never a limit of the machine, only of a milestone that had not been built, and it refused **34 of shv2's own functions**. Arguments past a register file now travel in stack slots on x64 and arm64, and wasm never had a limit to remove (its parameters are locals). What remains is a **STATED** ceiling with its own diagnostic — `MaxAbiArgs = 64`, the width of the per-argument float mask both ends of a call route through — and a **lower, separate** one for `async` spawns (`MaxAsyncArgs = 6`, the green thread's inline argument region, which the hand-assembled trampoline reads back into registers), also diagnosed where it used to be a compiler panic. ⭐ The rung's thesis: **ONE placement rule, consulted by both ends.** The callee's recomputing `computeParamSlotIndex` and each caller's running-counter twin of it were two spellings of one rule held together by a comment — survivable while every argument fit a register, and not survivable once "which slot" means either a register index within one FILE or an index into the single merged STACK area. Both reference compilers order it this way and say why.

A GT stack is `GtStackSize` = **0x800 (2 KB)** with `GtStackGuardMargin` = **0x3A0 (928 B)** of slack (`GtRuntime.maxon:191,200`), so the kernel's write runs off the end into unmapped memory and the process is gone before `X64Runtime`'s fault thunk — the thing that *prints* the panic — can execute. **⚠ THE 64 KB SYSTEM STACK DOES NOT AND CANNOT COVER THIS**, and that is the crux: `__gt_system_stack_top` solves **VOLUNTARY** kernel entry (the syscall shim picks the moment and switches RSP before a Win32 call); a fault is **INVOLUNTARY** — the CPU traps at an arbitrary instruction and there is no hook to switch stacks in first. shv2 has the system stack *and still dies*. **GO HIT THIS AND SOLVES IT TWICE:** on POSIX a per-M `sigaltstack` + `SA_ONSTACK` (the kernel switches stacks, so the small goroutine stack is never used); on Windows, where VEH has no altstack, it RESERVES the space via `_StackSystem` (`512*PtrSize` = **4 KB** on amd64) counted **TWICE** — in the allocation (`_FixedStack0 = _StackMin + _StackSystem`) *and* in the guard (`_StackGuard = 928*mult + _StackSystem`) so morestack fires while the reserve is intact. **shv2 carried over Go's `_StackMin` (2048) and the `928`, but NOT `_StackSystem`** — the one term that exists for exactly this — the same omission the C# bootstrap made (`GtLayout.cs`; see `docs/DEBUGGER_DESIGN.md` **P4d-GT-STACK**, where it was found as *"a breakpoint on a green-thread stack kills the debuggee"*). **CANDIDATE FIX, CHEAPER THAN GO'S — a PROPOSAL for the rung to validate, NOT a measured design:** map a small red zone below each GT stack sized for the kernel's pre-handler write (~1.5 KB ⇒ one page) so that write lands in MAPPED memory, and have the fault thunk switch RSP to `__gt_system_stack_top` as its FIRST action and run the handler body there. Go must fold a full 4 KB into every goroutine stack because it has no pre-existing system stack to hand off to; shv2 does, so it may pay one page per GT instead of inflating every stack — the system stack earning its keep twice. Whatever is chosen, the footprint is a **global per-GT memory tradeoff and must be MEASURED, not asserted**. ⚠ **shv2's exposure is STRICTLY LARGER than the bootstrap's**: the bootstrap forbids unguarded division statically (`E3103` when foldable, else `E3057` demanding `try/otherwise` or a non-zero ranged type), so safe bootstrap code cannot even reach a `#DE`; shv2 has no such check yet and `safety.md` deliberately specifies a *runtime* panic — so ordinary safe shv2 code reaches it today. **Acceptance when sequenced:** the `async` twin of `safety.md`'s divide-by-zero panics with a correct symbolized trace and exit 1; plus the arm64 question answered (POSIX `sigaltstack` is the right shape there, and the bootstrap already does it for its fault handler but NOT its debug trap handler).

The generated destructor was dumped at baseline and at that tree and **diffed: it is correct** (the two new cases carry only an int and an enum, get no arm, and the only change is one `check_` block's `jne` retargeting). 31 generated functions changed, all plausible match-arm and `rawValue`-chain extensions. **NOT a raw case-count limit** — a synthetic 112-case union does not reproduce it; something about *this* union's shape. ⇒ **Anyone adding a `TargetOp` variant will hit it and will have no reason to suspect the bootstrap.** Wave 2 sidesteps it entirely (the shipped design adds no union case, per the coordinator's correction to copy arm64's slot mechanism), so it is filed unblocked and unowned.
- **⚠ A `bool` CLOSURE PARAMETER TRAPS ON WASM — `wasm trap: indirect call type mismatch` (exit 3).** Found 2026-07-25 by the 2b-iii review while probing bool routes; **PRE-EXISTING** (reproduces on the pre-rung compiler) and **not this rung's**. Minimal repro: `let pass = function(x bool) gives x` then `pass(true)` — x64 exit **0**, wasm exit **3**. An `int` closure parameter is fine; a **named** function value with a `bool` param is fine. **ROOT CAUSE, both halves read:** `Targets/Wasm/StdToWasm.maxon:472` (`indirectCallParamValTypes`) declares every non-float indirect-call param **i64**, and `Runtime/FnRefThunk.maxon:200` (`thunkUserParamStdType`) normalizes every non-float param to `StdType.i64` — which is exactly why a **thunked** function value matches. A **LIFTED CLOSURE is not thunked**: it declares its source param types verbatim, so a `bool` param is `StdType.i1` → `wasmValTypeOf` → **i32**. The funcref's real type is `(i32, i64) → i64` while the `call_indirect` immediate says `(i64, i64) → i64`. ⭐ **The stated defect: the param model is TWO-valued (float / not-float) where the truth is THREE-valued (f64 / i32 / i64).** The suite is green over it only because no wasm-enabled closure spec uses a `bool` parameter. **Belongs to the P1.5-A1/A2 function-value workstream**, not to conformance.
- **⚠ FLOAT AS A GENERIC TYPE ARGUMENT PANICS THE BACKEND — `X64Backend.maxon:703`, xmm0 → rcx crosses register files.** Filed 2026-07-25; **PRE-EXISTING and coordinator-reproduced on the base**: `type Box uses T` + `typealias FBox = Box with float` + `FBox.create(2.5)`, **with no `where` clause at all**, panics. A float in an opaque `T` slot has no float-aware marshalling. ⚠ **2b-iii WIDENS THE DOOR, and the filed scope must say so:** admitting `float` to `Comparable`/`Equatable` means `Pair with Decimal where T is Comparable` — which was a clean **E3017** on base — now reaches that same panic, and **the constrained spelling is the one a user is most likely to write**. Neither form miscompiles (both fail the build) and the panic names the real gap, which is why it did not hold the rung. **The cure IS this rung's deliverable**: float-aware marshalling for an opaque `T`, plus a positioned diagnostic for the shapes that remain unsupported — which would land on `Box with float` too. Adjacent to the Std-tier bitcast that `float.hash` needs.
- **⚠ A NUMERIC-LITERAL METHOD RECEIVER MIS-LEXES — `7.hash()` and `1.5.equals(1.5)`.** Filed 2026-07-25; **PRE-EXISTING, and BOTH compilers reject it** (shv2: *"'if' requires a bool condition, got 'float'"*; the bootstrap: `E2010 Expected characterliteral`). `Lexer.maxon:972-1030`'s number scanner treats a `.` after digits as a decimal point unconditionally and then swallows a SECOND dot into the literal. - **⚠ A USER `type String` SHADOWS THE SYNTHESIZED `String.hash`/`String.equals` CONFORMER, AND IT COMPILES — LAST-WINS, NOT A DIAGNOSTIC.** Filed 2026-07-25 by the coordinator; surfaced (and MEASURED) by the direct-primitive-dispatch rung, but **pre-existing on the WITNESS path since Slice C**. `TypeResolution.isCompilerOwnedTypeName` (`:189`) refuses a user declaration that mints a nominal identity under `ExitCode`/`HashValue`/`Ordering` (2b-ii, E2015) — **but NOT under `String`.** So a user `type String` with its own `hash()` legally mints the symbol `String.hash`, which is the exact name `BuiltinConformanceRuntime` installs its synthesized djb2 body under (`qualifiedMethodName(StringConformerName, …)`). That rung cured its own *install* side (candidates narrowed to symbols the module does not already define), so the collision is currently masked rather than fixed. ⭐⭐ **AND IT IS A REACHABLE `0xC0000005`, NOT MERELY A WRONG ANSWER — measured by the dispatch rung's independent review, and ATTRIBUTED to the base by building `874e2f7bd` itself**: a user `type String` **plus** `Box with String where T is Hashable` FAULTS at runtime, **with or without a user `hash()` body**, identically on base. Root cause sits UPSTREAM of the install: `isIntrinsicBuiltinConformance` keys on the NAME `"String"`, so a user struct of that name is believed to conform intrinsically and is then handled as the builtin managed String RECORD — a struct pointer read through a fused-record layout it does not have. ⭐ **The proof that the synthesized body was silently replacing the user's**: at base both variants emit **2771 bytes, byte-identical whether or not the user wrote a `hash()`**; after the dispatch rung they differ (2695 vs 2771), i.e. the user's body is now the one that survives. ⇒ The `undefinedImplNames` narrowing is sound and this rung IMPROVES the case; **the name collision underneath remains, and it is a live segfault on `main` today.** ⚠ **`int` is structurally immune and that is the whole asymmetry**: `int` is a KEYWORD, so no user symbol can ever wear the `int.` qualifier — which is exactly why the dispatch rung scoped its widened `isCompilerInternalCallee` to `int.` only and deliberately left `String.*` out. **What the rung owes — this is a DESIGN CHOICE, not a bug fix, and the three options diverge:** (a) add `String` to `isCompilerOwnedTypeName`, refusing a user `type String` — symmetric with `Ordering`, but a sharper divergence from the bootstrap, which permits it because its stdlib is NAMESPACED (`stdlib.String.hash`) and shv2 has no namespacing; (b) give the synthesized conformer a distinguishable symbol — but it must stay nameable by a `funcAbs64` witness reloc, which is why it is not `__`-prefixed today; (c) keep both symbols legal and make the collision a DIAGNOSTIC rather than a silent last-wins. ⇒ Whichever is chosen, **the silent last-wins must not survive**: it is a wrong answer that no committed test reaches. **RELATED ASYMMETRY, accepted for now and recorded so a reader does not trip over it:** an `ExitCode`-tagged receiver does not dispatch — `ExitCode` is `int(0 to u32.max)` but carries its OWN value tag, and `canonicalizeRangedAlias`/`rangedAliasTag` reduce only `named` types, so `let a as ExitCode = 3` then `a.compare(b)` falls to the pre-existing clean E2015 while `Integer`/`Byte`/bare `int` all dispatch. (`10 as ExitCode` is unaffected — an int→int cast keeps the value's `integer` tag.)

- **✅✅ #40 → CONDITIONAL OWNERSHIP OF A BORROWED MANAGED-AGGREGATE PARAM RE-BOUND TO A `var` — CLOSED 2026-07-23 (main `7057bf8ad` fix + `b9f13dcac` review, on `134600b69`; suite 1366/0, `--workers=1`==`12` byte-identical, no 101). RESOLUTION: user ruled approach (A) RETAIN-PROMOTION. `var q = <borrowed aggregate param>` now emits `__mm_retain(p)` (NEW `MmRuntime` fn returning the ptr — `__mm_incref` returns void, so a returning twin was needed) so `q` co-owns the box from declaration: owned on every path (then/else/break/continue/loop-carried), aliasing preserved (`q.x=100` still shows through, matching the oracle), refcount balances. A BOUNDED refcount exception like COW #105. The parser promotes via a unified `promoteBorrowedToOwned` (review-consolidated declaration + reassignment dispatch), mirroring `promoteMutableString` but incref-not-copy. The `borrowedToOwned` branch that `ownedBindings.push`ed at the wrong depth is thereby dead on this path. 13 oracle-derived tests in `specs-shv2/conditional-ownership-param.md`. scale-test: #40's ISOLATED footprint is +0 allocs / +8 bytes (the one `usesRetain` bool) — proven by a post-merge A/B vs the parent `134600b69` (bit-identical absolute allocs), the printed row delta being the upstream perf commit `ffc521235`. Kept below as the closed technical record.** **What #40 actually was** (established 2026-07-23 by a reachability probe + an implementer stop-and-report, after the coordinator first *wrongly* concluded it unreachable): a borrowed struct/union **PARAMETER** (a P1.4a pass-by-reference value — its owned-heap bit unset) re-bound to a `var` (`var q = p`) is a borrowed managed var that SKIPS String promotion, so a later `q = <owned>` hits `reassignBindingValue`'s `borrowedToOwned` branch (`Parser.maxon:~6153`), which `ownedBindings.push`es `q` at the CURRENT block depth. When the reassignment is in a NESTED block, `q`'s owned value drops at the inner block's exit while `q` (declared outer) lives on → **use-after-free**. CONFIRMED RED under poison-on-free (#108): struct nested → **`0x3F3F3F3F`** (1061109567), union nested → **`0xC0000005`** fault, and the **`break` / `continue` / loop-carried / used-after-loop** variants all UAF too; oracle gives the correct value (9 / 7). **Same-depth reassign is BENIGN** (push depth == decl depth → exit 9). ⚠ **THE NAIVE FIX (drop `q` at its declaration scope) IS WRONG — it ships a NEW else-path double-free** (implementer-proven from emitted IR): after the merge `q` is a phi `{borrowed p (else), owned Point(9) (then)}`; an unconditional drop at function exit frees the borrowed `p` on the else-path, and the CALLER also decrefs that param → double-free. No committed spec exercises the else-path-taken case, so the suite stays green over it. ⚠ **COPY-PROMOTION (String's fix) IS ALSO WRONG** — a struct `var q = p` ALIASES the param box (`q.x = 100` shows through to the caller's `p`; verified both compilers), so copying diverges from the oracle. (`var q = <owned LOCAL>` is a MOVE on shv2 / rejected E3078 on the bootstrap — so this is PARAM-specific.) ⇒ **THE DESIGN RULING THE RUNG MUST CARRY (every correct fix breaks a thesis invariant — decide at sequencing):** **(A) retain-promotion** — `incref` the borrowed aggregate param at `var q = p` so `q` co-owns the box from declaration (owned on every path, aliasing preserved, refcount balances); a BOUNDED refcount exception like COW #105; needs `__mm_retain(ptr) returns ptr` in `MmRuntime.maxon` (today's `__mm_incref` returns void) + parser promotion mirroring String; **expands the "escape is the only place refcounts appear" thesis.** **(B) parser-side drop-flags** — a runtime "owns?" bool through every merge + conditional decref; no refcount but ADDS runtime flags, which the model deliberately avoids ("reconcile at joins, no flags"); larger, higher double-free/leak risk. **(C) reject** — diverges from the oracle (scope cut). Coordinator recommends (A). **Poison-on-free (#108) is the standing detector — the RED anchors + the `mutate(Point)`/`pick(Num)` probes reproduce it today.** Reachable via P1.4a's borrowed aggregate params, so P1.4a-adjacent.
- **⭐ Array slice COW — SLICE A ✅ CLOSED 2026-07-22 (`12705a7d9` + review `66bd13c24`, 1162→1171, 1184/0 after rebase); SLICE B (zero-copy slices) IS THE REMAINING P1.7 RESIDUAL.** (Number TBD — the parallel repo files #NN concurrently, so assign at sequencing to avoid a collision.) *(User ruling 2026-07-22: "COW makes slices nearly free… worked in as early as possible, a residual if it can be implemented immediately".)* **SLICED A/B by the coordinator after the survey, because A fixes live crashes and is a strict prerequisite for B.**
  - **✅ SLICE A — DETACH-ON-WRITE.** `__arr_cow_detach(record)` gives a record a private writable buffer before any in-place write; the only non-owned buffer at this slice is the `b"…"` literal's immortal `.rdata` blob (`capacity<0`). **It fixed FIVE reachable segfaults on valid programs**, none of which any spec covered: `set`/`clear`/`remove`/`pop` on a literal wrote into read-only `.rdata` (`0xC0000005`, empty stderr), and **`resize(-2)` wrote BELOW the buffer** (`-2 >= -2` satisfied grow's check so nothing detached) — on an owned array that silently erased the `__mm_alloc` header and published `count() == -1`, so it is now a clean abort (exit **73**), grounded in `stdlib/Array.maxon:11`'s `resize(newLength ElementCount)` where `ElementCount = int(0 to u64.max)`: the contract was always non-negative, shv2 just was not asserting it. Expected values all taken from the RUNNABLE ORACLE. ⚠ **`/specs` has NO twin** — no corpus case mutates a byte-string literal, and `codegen-internals.md`'s `rdata-cow-*` family covers `let arr = [1,2,3]` constant arrays in `.rdata`, a route shv2 does not have — so the 9 cases are authored (precedent: the shv2-only `push-grows-off-rdata`), oracle-valued.
  - **⭐ THE CHECK LIVES IN THE EMITTED RUNTIME FUNCTION, NOT AT THE CALL SITES — a deliberate divergence from BOTH references, and the slice's thesis.** Both refs emit a COW check per mutation site and **both have holes because that list drifted**: the bootstrap's `clear` and `setLength` mutate a shared buffer with *no check at all* (`MaxonToStandardConversion.ManagedMemory.cs:1654`, `:1588`), and v1's `shift_left`/`shift_right` are saved only by an arithmetic accident. Putting the detach inside `__arr_*` makes "every mutation site is gated" a property of the runtime instead of a checklist. **Gating rule, stated once: a mutator either calls `__arr_grow` (whose FIRST op is an unconditional detach, ahead of its own `capacity >= required` early-out) or calls the detach itself.** ⇒ 5 call sites (`grow`/`set`/`clear`/`remove`/`pop`) gate all 9 mutators; a 6th in `insert` would be an unreachable branch. Verified adversarially via the INTERNED-TWIN test (mutate one `b"hey"`, read the other — rdata intact).
  - **✅ SLICE B — ZERO-COPY SLICES — CLOSED 2026-07-22** (`14a0aaa75` + review `cd77c6805`, 1184→**1199/0**). `.slice`/`.clone` return a VIEW: own 48-byte record, `buffer@0 = base + start·element_size` (**INTERIOR**), `capacity@16 = -1` (view sentinel, distinct from `-2` rdata), `parent@32` = the **BASE pointer `__mm_alloc` returned** (the base, not the parent RECORD — `__mm_decref` needs the header at `base-24`, and an interior pointer would read the parent's DATA). **`__mm_incref` returned**, installed by `installArrayRuntime` since the view is its only caller — the consumer `MmRuntime.maxon:362-380` had been waiting for. `__arr_cow_detach` gained **ARM 2** (an owner whose buffer's refcount is non-zero detaches too) exactly as slice A promised: another arm of the SAME test, **no call site touched**. `__arr_decref`/`__arr_grow` now `__mm_decref` the shared base instead of `__mm_free`. **Nested views FLATTEN** — a view's `parent@32` is always the ORIGINAL base, never another record, so there is no chain and nothing walks one. Managed elements stay E2015-rejected (see the trap below).
    **⭐ MEASURED, by the coordinator, not claimed:** 500 slices of a 200k array **469 ms → 15 ms**, and *doubling the slice size doubles the OLD time while the new stays flat* — O(n)→O(1), asymptotic not constant-factor. Optimizer confirmed depth-independence (2,000,000 slices at nesting depth 1/10/100/1000 → 121/97/107/98 ms; a chain walk would make depth 1000 ~1000× slower) and length-independence (~50 ns/slice, flat across 100×).
    **⭐ THE SABOTAGE THAT MATTERED:** deleting the incref turned **19 tests red** including `slice-outlives-its-parent` (exit **101**) — and exactly the three base-0 cases stayed green (`slice-of-empty-array-then-push`, `slice-of-byte-string-literal`, `clone-of-byte-string-literal`), which is correct: they owe no incref. The gate was seen RED before it was believed.
    ⚠⚠ **A SECOND SABOTAGE DID *NOT* GO RED, AND THAT IS THE MORE IMPORTANT FINDING** — see #108. Moving the buffer release *ahead* of the copy in `__arr_cow_detach` still passed 1197/0, because `__mm_free` reclaims nothing under the bump allocator, so the "freed" bytes read back intact. The spec prose claiming *"a release before the copy would read freed bytes"* was **FALSE AS WRITTEN** and was corrected: the ordering is a rule the function KEEPS, not one a gate PROTECTS. It becomes load-bearing the day the allocator reuses memory.
    ⚠ **`scale-test` MOVED and is attributed**: +78 allocs / +3,566 bytes / +24 `.text` bytes **FLAT at every rung** — proven by A/B (restoring the old threaded `emitRefcountCheckToLastOwner` shape returns every rung to the previous numbers EXACTLY) to be the 5 Std ops `emitAdjustRefcount` adds to `__mm_decref`'s `lower` block, at the one reachable call site per module. Bought to put `owners - 1` and the refcount RMW in ONE function each now that `__arr_cow_detach` reads that convention across a file boundary. Row written to `docs/optimization-log.md`.
  - ⚠⚠ **THE "REFERENCE TO PORT" PREMISE THIS ENTRY USED TO STATE IS MEASURED FALSE (survey 2026-07-22).** It said to port bootstrap `LowerManagedMemSlice`+`EmitCowCheck` and v1 `__managed_mem_slice`/`__managed_mem_cow_check`. **NEITHER reference has ever zero-copied a slice of an OWNED array.** v1's `__managed_mem_slice` (`stdlib/Internals.maxon:3818`) is an EAGER COPY (`parent = ROOT`, `capacity = sliceLen`) — its `capacity == -1` sentinel is *tested everywhere and produced nowhere*. The bootstrap views only IMMUTABLE sources (rdata `-2`, or another view `-1`) and **refuses** an owned one, in its own comment (`Strings.cs:1480`): *"heap-allocated source cannot be zero-copy because struct-level COW can't distinguish slice refs from normal refs."* Its parent-side detacher `maxon_cow_struct_detach` (`RuntimeEmitter.MemoryManager.cs:1402`) tests `refcount != 1`, is emitted into every binary, and is **CALLED FROM NOWHERE** — that dead function IS the "one-directional hole", and `docs/MEMORY_MANAGEMENT.md:474` documents it as if it were live. ⇒ **Slice B is a NEW DESIGN, not a port.**
  ⭐ **THE ONE DESIGN FORK a move-only compiler forces (settled for B by the survey):** a shared view must keep the parent's buffer ALIVE while it references it. **(A) REFCOUNT the shared buffer** — a bounded, deliberate exception to "no runtime refcount", ONLY for COW-shared array buffers. **(B) BORROW-LIVENESS (E3070)** — a compile-time-bounded borrow that provably can't outlive the parent; purer vs the thesis, but forbids slice-outlives-parent. ⇒ **pairs with the E3070 residual + the borrow-on-get thesis — one design thread.** **⇒ TAKE (A), ANCHORED ON THE BUFFER, NOT THE RECORD — and that is precisely why shv2 can do what neither reference could.** Both refs refcount the RECORD, where a count of 2 cannot distinguish *"two owners"* from *"someone views my buffer"* — exactly why the bootstrap gave up. **shv2's array buffer is a SEPARATE `__mm_alloc` allocation whose own refcount slot at `buffer-8` is currently always 0 and read by nothing** (`MmRuntime.maxon:48`, `ArrayRuntime.maxon:744-746`), so a non-zero count there means one thing only: someone is viewing these bytes. shv2 gets that unambiguous signal **because** it is move-only. `__mm_incref` returns here, which is the caller `MmRuntime.maxon:362-380` explicitly anticipates. ⚠ Keep the E2015 rejection of MANAGED slice/clone/append: v1's `cow_check` does **no element retain** and is sound only because its two reachable triggers stamp `element_destroy = 0` — a managed-element view detaching shallowly is a double-free (v1 `Internals.maxon:3843-3849` names the UAF it already paid for).
- **#103 — builtin array methods do not enforce their RANGED parameter types, so every bounds guard is hand-written.**
  `Parser.parseArrayOneArg` types a builtin array method's argument as plain `integer`, so `stdlib/Array.maxon`'s
  `ElementIndex` / `ElementCount = int(0 to u64.max)` are not applied at the call site. That is *why* `get`/`set`/
  `remove`/`insert`/`slice` each carry a runtime `emitIsNegative` guard and why `resize` needed a new one (#102,
  abort 73) — shv2's `StdCmpPred` has no unsigned compare, so a negative slips every signed `>=` test. **A
  compile-time rejection at the call site would SUBSUME all of them** and turn a class of runtime aborts into
  E3005s. Front-end (parser + P1.9's range machinery), orthogonal to the array runtime. *(Surfaced by the COW
  slice-A rung; it is the generalization of the five segfaults that rung fixed one at a time.)*
- **✅ #104 — runtime ABORT exit codes now have ONE home, and the duplicate check IS THE LANGUAGE — CLOSED 2026-07-22** (main `0be8c7465`). The whole space became a single `RuntimeAbort` `enum`, so two cases sharing a raw value is `E3030`/`E3031` **from the bootstrap that compiles shv2** — no hand-written checker to rot, verified RED before relying on it. The 70/70 collision (`GtRuntime.ProcStoreOverflowExitCode` vs `ArrayRuntime.ElementSizeZeroExitCode`) was resolved by moving the array's unreachable `elementSizeZero` 70→74 (GT's 70 is spec-pinned); `101` (leak gate) and `134` (`userPanic`) folded in as reserved cases. `emitVoidAbort`'s `osExit`+dead-terminator fact single-homed as `emitRuntimeAbort`, which **derives the terminator from `func.returnType`** (so a caller cannot pick the wrong one), folding in `GtRuntime`'s two open-codings AND `buildArrCreate`'s value-returning twin (a prior review's "keep it separate" finding overturned on its own terms — it was conditioned on being the file's only value-returning abort, and `__gt_process_run` is a second). ⚠ Residual: `SpecWorkerPool.LeakCheckExitCode = 101` stays spelled locally BY DESIGN — a worker is the shv2 binary compiled by the C# bootstrap, so its 101 is `maxon-sharp`'s leak gate, not this enum's; the review corrected the note that framed it as an unresolved copy.

New `Compiler/Runtime/BufferOwnership.maxon`: **`capacity@16 < 0` ⇒ "not mine to write or release"** (the negative records only provenance — `ViewBufferCapacity -1`, `RdataBufferCapacity -2`, `InlineBufferCapacity -3`); **`parent@32` ⇒ "which separate allocation do I owe a `__mm_decref`"** or `NoOwedAllocation` (0). - **✅ #107 — `try` binds the OUTERMOST call of a postfix chain — CLOSED 2026-07-22** (main `83d072d35`, →1308/0). The size comes from the header (`HeaderSizeOffset`), so the range is exactly the payload. **The whole class this was filed for is now a STANDING GATE**: the committed suite runs under poison on every spec run. **PROVEN TO HAVE TEETH, not merely green** (a gate is not evidence until seen RED): moving `__str_append`'s release ahead of its blit (the #43 bug) made `var s="abc"; s.append(s); s.append(s)` print `abcabc??????` under poison, restored → `abcabcabcabc`; the review independently re-proved RED with a different `__str_decref` sabotage (`0xC0000005` fault). **Suite 1308/0 under poison** — no committed test masks a UAF the suite reaches. Now permanent.)*
