## Register allocator — the DEAD-DEF pressure hole ✅ CLOSED 2026-07-28

✅ **A DEAD DEF HOLDS A REGISTER, AND NO LIVE SET COULD EVER SEE IT — DONE, MERGED** (impl `eccbf31f4` · review `bf2324a6d`; x64-windows **2071→2084/0**, x64-linux **1978/0**, wasm **1971/0**, builds 0 warnings, no 101, `verify-warm-rebuild` PASS, and the whole suite **2084/0 under a `VerifyIncrementalSplit = true` build**; arm64 SKIP — remote, UNVERIFIED, but byte-compared, see below).

⚠⚠ **THE FILED PREMISE WAS A SYMPTOM, NOT THE BUG — the fourth filing this session to be wrong about its own defect.** It read *"an INDIRECT call of arity ≥ 14 panics the register allocator"*, and the coordinator's brief carried an `N+1` arithmetic (N arguments + the callee address) that **gets the right number from the wrong mechanism**. The implementer disproved it by instrumenting, and the coordinator verified the correction on unmodified `main`: **15 parameters with the last one unused PANICS; 14 compiles — with no function value anywhere.**

**THE REAL DEFECT:** a virtual def that is **live at no program point** is absent from every live-before/live-after set, so it is **invisible to every popcount over a live set** — but **its register is real** (`mov rax, [rbp+96]` clobbers rax whatever becomes of the value, and `allocateDef` runs for every def, dead or not). So `analyzePressure` under-counts by one, `peak.found` goes false with the point still over pool, and the **COLORER** panics (`RegisterAllocator.maxon:1173`) *after the splitter believed it was finished* — violating the allocator's stated contract (`RegisterAllocator.maxon:47-56`: after splitting "coloring CANNOT fail"). ⭐ **`maxPressure`, the supposedly INDEPENDENT post-condition cross-check, has the identical hole**, so it did not fire either — though it agrees *by construction* (one implementation), which is why the rung did not need to fix it twice. Indirect calls merely sat one arity lower because **`__fnref_` thunks add a `__env` parameter the author never wrote and the thunk never reads.**

**THE FIX:** `addReuseTransientPressure` → `addOpTransientPressure`, answering both halves of one question — *"does this op's def need a register this op does not free?"* — i.e. the existing reuse-copy transient **plus +1 when the op's plain virtual def is absent from live-after and no virtual use dies there**. A def that IS live after is charged nothing, being already billed as live-before at the next op, which is why every previously-compiling program emits identical instructions. ⭐ **It is the op-def twin of the dead-PHI reservation — only the phi half existed.** A known pattern with one half missing is this file's most reliable bug signature.

⭐⭐ **THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW FOUND THE FIX INCOMPLETE, AND THE PANIC STILL REACHABLE** (`bf2324a6d`). The new charge was **CLASS-BLIND**: `anyVirtualUseDiesAt` scored a dying operand of the *other register file* as relief for a dead def that cannot inherit it — `blocked = (working ∖ dyingRegs) ∪ forbidden ∪ (fullRegisterMask ∖ classPool)` names every dying register whatever its file, and `classPool` then puts the foreign ones straight back. **So a dying XMM counted as relief for a dead GPR def.** Measured three ways (`main` / rung HEAD / after fix) with real exit codes: a **99-program sweep (9 op shapes × arities 10–20) fails 7 on the rung's HEAD** — `f2i` at *every* arity from 14 to 20, the whole cliff, not an edge. Coordinator-verified independently: a 17-float dead-tail panics on `main` and compiles on the branch. **The rung's own committed cases were all same-file, which is exactly why a green suite stood over it.**

⭐⭐ **AND THE DUPLICATION WAS THE LOAD-BEARING KIND, DEMONSTRATED IN REAL TIME.** `refreshTransientAt` (the incremental repair) was a **SECOND IMPLEMENTATION of the same decision in a second file** — *"is the def dead? does the op free a register?"* asked against the use index instead of a bitset — with nothing forcing the copies to agree and `VerifyIncrementalSplit`, **compiled out by default**, the only thing that would ever catch a divergence. **The proof it mattered is that the review's one-conjunct class fix had to be applied to BOTH copies.** It now supplies only the liveness oracle and calls the single decision procedure. **De-duplicating cost exactly ZERO** — all six scale rungs identical in allocations, bytes *and* `codeBytes` against the pre-review binary.

**COSTS:** allocations went **DOWN** (−43 / −191 / −487 / −1,079 / −2,263 at rungs 1–5) — the `ScannedValues.split` box `refreshSplitTransients` no longer builds; `regalloc:splitting` ratios 1.98–2.18, linear. ⚠ Rung 0's +31/+2,733 is the **worktree path length**, not a change. **CODEGEN IS BYTE-IDENTICAL on both targets**, byte-compared with a **same-binary CONTROL column** (x64-windows 9 programs, arm64-macos 4 programs, 0 differences and 0 control differences).

⚠ **THE 4 MODIFIED GOLDENS ARE PURE SPILL-SLOT RENUMBERING, VERIFIED NOT ASSERTED** — an op now reporting its true demand outranks one it used to tie with, so victims receive slots in a different order. Normalising ONLY the slot number (registers and mnemonics intact), the removed and added line multisets are **IDENTICAL**, slot counts unchanged and the distinct slot-ID *sets* identical (13/24/16/11). The same four tests' **x64-linux** goldens owed the identical permutation and were regenerated unfiltered (70 lines, zero unmatched).

⚠ **THE SCALE CORPUS IS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO THE CLASS FIX** — it is int-only, so it contains **zero cross-class dead defs**. The identical-allocation result proves the *de-duplication* costs nothing and says **nothing** about the class fix; what covers that is the four review-added spec cases and the 99-program sweep. **The reviewer stated this itself rather than letting the Δ0 imply coverage it does not have.**

**CORPUS GAP THAT LET IT SHIP:** the maximum arity anywhere in either corpus is **22 (DIRECT)**; the maximum **INDIRECT** arity was **2**. The corpus had never come within an order of magnitude of the cliff. 13 authored cases now pin it — the mechanism (dead defs, **no function value anywhere**) in `register-pressure.md`, the symptom (indirect arity 13/14/20/26, plus arity 20 with **computed** arguments, since literal arguments are relieved free by remat) in `first-class-functions.md`, and the **arm64 boundary at 27 params** ungated so it runs on both lanes — verified to genuinely exercise the fix (it panics on `main` under `--target=arm64-macos`).

**⇒ THREE RESIDUALS FILED:** · ⬜ **`__fnref_` thunks materialize a `__env` parameter they never read** (`Compiler/Runtime/FnRefThunk.maxon:153`) — a **compiler-introduced surplus value invisible to the author**, which is what pushed the arity boundary down by one for every function value. Post-fix it is no longer a panic but costs a **store + reload in every thunk of user arity ≥ 13**. ⭐ Reviewer's shape note, adopted: the rung is **NOT** *"remove `__env`"* (closures need the slot) but *"a materialized parameter with no uses should not be materialized"* — a DFE/lowering question, in `Compiler/Runtime/`, not `Targets/`. · ⬜ **`phase:parse` is SUPERLINEAR IN CPU while LINEAR IN ALLOCATIONS** — coordinator-measured at `--repeat=3` (min-of-3, so not a noise sample): ratios **1.80 → 2.23 → 2.48 → 3.00 → 3.14** across the doubling ladder, against parse allocations of 1.85 → 1.99. At rung 5 parse is **13.0e9 ticks against regalloc's 14.0e9** — nearly the whole compile. This rung runs *after* parse and cannot have caused it. **This is exactly the cost class the CPU column was added to make visible**, and it is invisible to the memory columns by construction. **RE-MEASURE TRIGGER: any parser change; confirm at `--repeat=3` before acting.** · ⬜ **`verify-warm-rebuild maxon-shv2/track0` is BROKEN on `main`** — `track0/alloc-torture.maxon:47` calls `__Builtins.parallelBoundary`, which no longer exists (**E3004**). Reproduced on `main`; track0 cannot serve as that gate's target until repaired.

⚠⚠ **STANDING TRAP, NOW THIRD-TIME-CONFIRMED IN ONE SESSION: A COMPARISON WITHOUT A CONTROL IS NOT A MEASUREMENT.** The reviewer's first byte-compare read *"16 of 16 DIFFER"* — because it wrote the two artifacts to different output paths and **the image embeds its own output path**. It self-corrected by adding a **same-binary control column**, which read 0 and proved the harness sound. The same path-length family has now caught **an optimizer, a reviewer, and the coordinator** in this session alone. ⇒ **Every A/B carries a same-binary control, and the control is run BEFORE any difference is reported.**

## `phase:parse` — the Θ(vars × constructs) bend ✅ CLOSED 2026-07-28

✅ **THE PARSE BEND WAS Θ(VARS IN SCOPE × MERGING CONSTRUCTS), AND IT ALLOCATED NOTHING — DONE, MERGED** (optimize `88ca97b33`; x64-windows **2142/0**, x64-linux PASS, wasm **2029/0**, builds 0 warnings, no 101, `verify-warm-rebuild` PASS, **`specs-shv2/fragments/` EMPTY after a full run**; arm64 SKIP — remote, UNVERIFIED).

**THE READING THAT FOUND IT — off the doubling ladder, at `--repeat=3`.** `phase:parse` was the **ONLY** superlinear phase: CPU **×2.02 → 2.29 → 2.57 → 2.86 → 3.24** per doubling while its **allocations stayed linear** (1.85 → 1.99), and every other phase was linear in CPU (lex 1.84–2.01, signatures 1.84–2.04, isel 1.85–1.90, regalloc 1.93–2.19). Parse's share of compile CPU was climbing **14.4% → 37.5%** while regalloc fell 51.6% → 40.5% — **on that trajectory parse overtakes the register allocator at the next rung.** ⭐ **A cost that bends in CPU while flat in allocations ALLOCATES NOTHING**, which is exactly the class the CPU column was added to expose, and why the memory columns read flat over this for the project's whole history.

**THE BEND, NAMED:** `Parser.assignedBindingsIn` (`Parser.maxon:13402`). Every `if`/`match`/`while`/`for` asks which mutable bindings its token extent assigns; the old answer walked the **entire** `mutableVars` list and probed each binding's name against a per-construct `Set` — one `ByteArray` hash per binding in scope, per construct. `Parser.mintLoopHeaderPhis` had the same shape for the loop half. **Instrumented on the corpus BEFORE any change: 39,400,068 probes at rung 5 across 18,571 constructs, ×3.99 per doubling — and `maxA = 2`. It was scanning 4,102 bindings to select two.**

⭐ **THE METHOD IS THE LESSON.** The corpus doubles *both* axes at once and structurally cannot separate them, so a new ladder did: `maxon-shv2/Testing/ladders/genscope.sh` (constructs / locals / both / a `straight` control), committed and **indexed in that directory's README**. Constructs alone ×1.72–1.89, locals alone ×1.46–1.83, **both ×2.21–2.83**, straight control ×1.80–1.89 — only the product bends. Then the diagnosis was **confirmed before anything was designed**, by capping the walk at 8 entries: bend gone, allocations unchanged to the digit.

**THE FIX:** an inverse index on the parser — `mutableVarInnermost` (name → innermost position) and `mutableVarShadowed` (per position, the position it shadows) — pushed/popped in lockstep under the existing `openBlock` mark, copy-on-written off shared empties. Θ(vars × constructs) ⇒ **Θ(tokens in the extent + assigned)**. `namesAssignedIn` and its per-construct `Set` are **deleted**, and `mintLoopHeaderPhis` takes the same carried list — **the two orderings that had to agree are now one.**

⚠⚠ **THE RISK HERE IS CORRECTNESS, NOT SPEED: THE CARRIED SET'S ORDER DECIDES PHI ORDER.** The claim the whole change rests on is that *positions are collected ASCENDING, ascending position IS `mutableVars` declaration order, so there is no sort and no reordering — and the shadow chain is what keeps it exact.* A mistake there **miscompiles**; it does not merely run slower.

**RESULTS (path-clean A/B, parent and fix built in the same worktree at the same path, `--repeat=3`):** rung-5 parse CPU **13,160,151,600 → 3,354,949,049 (−74.5%, 3.92×)**; whole-compile CPU **35.87G → 24.78G (−30.9%)**. **Coordinator-verified independently on the merged branch: parse ratios now ×1.71 1.95 1.94 2.03 2.00 — LINEAR — and parse's share reads 14.0% → 13.6% ACROSS the ladder instead of climbing to 37.5%.** Same-binary control: allocations and bytes bit-identical, CPU spread −5.5%…+0.5%, so the noise band is ~6% and a 3.9× is nowhere near it.

**MEMORY — exactly two phases moved and the arithmetic closes:** `phase:parse` −4,060 … −143,487 allocations and −9,493,072 bytes at rung 5 (the per-construct `Set`, ~7.7 allocations each); `phase:signatures` **+0 allocations**, +35,760 bytes — the `Parser` record grew 16 bytes for two pointer fields, and 1,536/16 = 96 = the 30 files plus 66 top-level constants that phase builds a `Parser` for. **−9,493,072 + 35,760 = −9,457,312, the total.** (An unconditional `create()` pair first measured **+13,410** allocations there; the shared-empty COW is why it is now zero.)

⚠⚠ **THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW DID NOT COMPLETE — it died on a hard weekly API limit mid-investigation, and its report is lost.** Its *measurements* survive in the worktree and are strong; the coordinator then closed the four checks it had not reached. **Recorded as a process deviation, not papered over.**
- ⭐ **What the review DID establish, and it is the load-bearing evidence: a 250-case DIFFERENTIAL FUZZ against a control worktree pinned at the exact parent commit (`3f2e3203f`)**, generating precisely the shapes that stress the index — many mutable bindings (wide carried sets), **the same name re-declared at several nesting depths (shadow chains)**, merging constructs assigning random subsets **in deliberately inverted order**, and shadows popped with the outer binding carried by a later construct. It compared the build exit code, **the emitted binary BYTE-FOR-BYTE**, and **runtime stdout + exit code**: **130 compiled clean on both, 0 mismatches.** It also ran `verify-warm-rebuild` on a shadow-heavy program: PASS.
- **Coordinator-closed afterwards:** `namesAssignedIn` is **fully deleted** (zero occurrences ⇒ one door); the **shared-empty COW is safe** (`if self.mutableVarShadowed is sharedEmptyMutableVarShadowed` swaps in fresh arrays *before* any push, so the shared empty is never written through); **lockstep violations PANIC loudly** rather than corrupting silently (*"the shadow column ran out before `mutableVars` did — the two grew apart"*); and the **closure-lifting path saves/restores both index fields AS A UNIT with `mutableVars`**, so the index travels with the thing it indexes.
- **Corpus-wide codegen neutrality is the other pillar:** `specs-shv2/fragments/` **empty after a full suite run** on x64, with x64-linux and wasm both PASS — for a change that decides phi order, byte-identical goldens across ~2,142 programs is the strongest available evidence.

**⇒ THREE ITEMS FILED, each with its numbers:** · ⬜ **The token scan still walks token-by-token**, so a construct nested D deep has its tokens re-read by all D enclosing scans (`LoopNestBase`, isolated by `gennest.sh`). ⭐ The optimizer also **corrected a stale claim** in `blockStatementEndIndex` that inverting the scan costs ×3.5 — that figure had been measured when its constant was multiplied by the Θ(V) walk now removed, **so it no longer stands in either direction and the question is open.** · ⬜ **`desugarTry` snapshots the whole `mutableVars` per `try`** (`Parser.maxon:10039`, `10284`) — the **same O(V×C) shape, in time AND bytes**. ⚠ **The scale corpus generates no `try`**, so it is unmeasured and explicitly unclaimed; it is the obvious next thing to point `genscope.sh` at. · **MEASURED DEBT (Workstream O):** the ordered insert is O(A²) in 4-byte shifts where the old walk was O(V) in hash probes — worst case measured by hand (A = V = 250/500/1000/2000, and 8 wide `if`s at V = 125…1000): **both stay linear, ×1.95–×2.03, costing +1%…+4%**. **RE-MEASURE TRIGGER: a rung that makes wide carried sets ordinary.**

## Workstream O — the compiler traces ITSELF ⭐

**Small, and it lands FIRST — it is a debugging instrument, and an instrument that arrives after
the bug is worthless.** shv2's `Logger` today formats a `String` and prints it to **stderr**. That
survives exactly as long as the compiler is single-threaded. **P1.0a interleaves N workers into one
stderr**, and P1.5 puts green threads under them; at that point a text log is not degraded, it is
*useless* — you cannot tell which worker, which compilation unit, or which phase a line came from,
and the lines themselves are torn.

**The mechanism already exists — the bootstrap has all of it.** `maxon.exe` compiles binaries that
carry a shared-memory ring (128-byte header, 8-byte packed entry headers, ticket-spinlock reserve),
and `maxon monitor` creates the segment, spawns the child with `MAXON_DEBUGSTREAM` set, drains the
ring, and decodes it — parsing real names out of a `MXDS_TAGS` blob in the PE. **shv2 is a Maxon
program compiled by `maxon.exe`, so it already runs under that monitor.** The one missing link:
the producer is wired only into *runtime internals* (mm / sched / dbg events). **Nothing lets user
Maxon source put an event into the ring.** That is the whole gap, and it is a builtin.

⇒ **Workstream O does NOT depend on Workstream R.** It is not blocked on the shv2 runtime, on
ownership, or on `String`. It can land against the compiler as it stands *today*.

**Two tiers, because the hot tier must not allocate.** A formatted-text log inside the register
allocator would (a) allocate into the very `mm` stream you are trying to read and (b) cost more
than the work it is measuring. `Logger`'s `LazyMessage` thunk does not save you: the closure env is
built at the call site whether or not the level check passes.

- **Tier 1 — structured, ZERO-ALLOC.** Event code + fixed numeric args, exactly like the existing
  Dbg events. Names are **interned at compile time** into a `MXDS_STRS` PE blob (the `MXDS_TAGS`
  trick, reused), so an event carries a `u16` id and the monitor prints the real name. No `String`,
  no thunk, no allocation. **This is the tier the passes use.**
- **Tier 2 — text.** A length-prefixed UTF-8 tail for the rare human message. Allocating, and it
  says so. `entry_size` is a `u16`, so an entry caps at 64 KiB — truncate, never tear.

**Every event carries `gt` + `p_id`.** Obtained the way `EmitDbgCallCore` gets them (`LoadCurrentP`,
NULL-guarded). **This is the entire point of the workstream** — it is what lets the monitor demux N
workers back into per-worker, per-unit timelines instead of a shuffled pile. An event also carries
a `unit_id` (which fragment / which function), so a parallel harness run reads as one timeline per
unit rather than one per process.

**The schema is FROZEN — so these are NEW codes, in a free range** (`0x5F–0xFD` is unused):

| code | event | payload after the 8-byte entry header |
|---|---|---|
| `0x60` | `LOG_PHASE_BEGIN` | `gt`(8) · `p_id`(8) · `phase_id`(2) `rsvd`(2) `unit_id`(4) — 32B entry |
| `0x61` | `LOG_PHASE_END` | *(same)* |
| `0x62` | `LOG_EVENT` | `gt`(8) · `p_id`(8) · `cat`(1) `lvl`(1) `event_id`(2) `unit_id`(4) · `arg0`(8) · `arg1`(8) — 48B entry, the Dbg shape |
| `0x63` | `LOG_TEXT` | `gt`(8) · `p_id`(8) · `cat`(1) `lvl`(1) `len`(2) `unit_id`(4) · UTF-8 tail, zero-padded to 8 |

**Keep the two-tier gating, and inline the guard** — the rule ARCHITECTURE.md already states for
shv2's producer applies here from commit 1: compile-time (`--debugstream` off ⇒ **zero
instructions**), runtime (`__ds_base == 0` ⇒ inline bail, *before* any CALL). The C# producer's MM
events pay two real CALLs before the runtime-off check; do not reproduce that wart.

### The slices

- **O1 — NOW, before P1.0a.** A `__DebugStream` builtin in **`maxon-sharp`** (callable from Maxon
  source), the four event codes, the `MXDS_STRS` intern blob, a DebugStream **sink behind
  `Logger`'s existing category/level API** (the call sites do not change), and `maxon monitor
  --filter=log` decode. **No dependency on anything in Phase 1.**
- **O2 — with P1.0a.** `gt`/`p_id`/`unit_id` demux in the monitor: per-worker and per-unit
  timelines. The pool's first debugging tool exists the day the pool does — not a month after it.
- **O3 — inside R1 @ P1.2.** shv2's own backend emits the same builtin, so the trace **survives
  self-host**. This is not new work: it is an *obligation on* the DebugStream producer port R1
  already carries. Name it there or it will be forgotten.
- **O4 — ✅ LANDED 2026-07-25. The per-phase CPU-TIME column.** A `__Builtins.threadCpuTicks()`
  intrinsic in **`maxon-sharp`**, bracketed by shv2's `PhaseProbe`, surfaced in `--metrics`,
  `--log=compiler:debug` and `scale-test`. **This is the instrument the measured-debt list below
  asks for BY NAME** (*"an argument for the runtime/time instrument that does not exist yet"*,
  *"the strongest Workstream-O candidate on the board"*). Its own section follows.

### ⚠ It is also the replacement for a timing instrument P1.0a is about to BREAK

`CompileTimings`/`CompileMemory` accumulate into **global** per-phase timers. Under a worker pool
two workers are in different phases at once, and a global accumulator cannot express that — the
numbers do not just get noisy, they stop *meaning* anything. `LOG_PHASE_BEGIN`/`END` give properly
nested, per-worker, per-unit spans, and the disjoint-and-sums-to-total check gets computed **from
the trace** instead of from an accumulator that is structurally unable to be right. *(This is the
"a dominant cost hid in the wrong timing bucket" failure, four times over in v1, and the parallel
pool is about to make the bucket itself invalid.)*

**And the trace can be a GOLDEN.** Normalize it the way `mm-trace` already normalizes — drop the
timestamp, dense-renumber ids in first-appearance order — and the **worker-count-invariance gate**
at the Phase-1 GATE sharpens from "`-j1` and `-jN` agree on the *verdicts*" to "they agree on the
**per-unit event sequence**." That is a far tighter net, and it costs nothing extra to hold.

### ✅ O4 — THE PER-PHASE **CPU-TIME** COLUMN (2026-07-25). The instrument this list has been asking for by name.

**It spans both compilers, because neither half is enough alone:** `maxon-sharp` mints the intrinsic,
shv2 brackets it. **What it closes is a sentence this file writes about itself over and over** —
*"TIME-only and allocation-free, so `scale-test` STRUCTURALLY CANNOT SEE IT"*, *"no rung of this
ladder can ever show it"*, *"the strongest Workstream-O candidate on the board"*. Those were true,
and they are now out of date **as a limitation**; every measurement filed under them stands
untouched.

- **`__Builtins.threadCpuTicks()`** — bootstrap intrinsic, `QueryThreadCycleTime` on Windows (⇒ TSC
  ticks) and `clock_gettime(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID)` on macOS (⇒ nanoseconds). It reads CPU time
  consumed by the **CALLING THREAD ONLY**. **It cannot see preemption and it cannot see any other
  process**, which is precisely why it can be trended where wall time cannot. *(Verified
  empirically, not argued: across a 300 ms sleep it advanced **837,520 ticks** while wall time
  advanced **301,000,000 ns**.)*
- **`PhaseProbe` brackets it alongside the existing wall clock and memory counters**, so every
  `CompilePhase` and every `RegAllocPhase` reports a CPU cost. `--metrics=<path>`'s TSV gains a
  **7th, APPENDED** column `cputicks` (appended rather than slotted in beside `nanos`, so every
  existing field keeps its index). `scale-test` prints a **third** per-phase table beside
  allocations and bytes, and records a third table in `docs/optimization-log.md` under **`## CPU`**.
- **`--log=compiler:debug`'s timing table gains a `cpu%` beside the wall `%`** — and the pair is
  worth more than either column: **a phase where the two disagree spent its wall time NOT RUNNING.**
  Measured: `load` is **51.2% of wall but 25.4% of CPU** because it waits on file IO, while
  `regalloc` is **22.2% of wall and 36.1% of CPU**.

⚠ **THE HONEST LIMITS. State them, because a column read as if it were the allocation column would
be worse than no column at all.**

- **CPU ticks are NOT bit-reproducible the way allocations are.** They move with turbo, thermal
  throttling and cache pressure from other cores — **a few percent** — so **a movement inside that
  band is not a datapoint**. Against the only question a doubling ladder asks (**×2 linear vs ×4
  quadratic**) that band has a **100% margin**, which is exactly why it is good enough here and
  worth nothing against a claimed 3% constant factor. **The memory columns keep their stronger
  property: any movement at all is real.**
- **The unit is platform-defined and the platforms do not agree** (TSC ticks vs nanoseconds), and
  there is **no honest conversion** — `QueryPerformanceFrequency` is the *performance counter's*
  rate, not the TSC's. ⇒ **Compare RATIOS between rungs, which are unit-free, or absolutes only
  within one platform.**
- **Wall-clock nanos are still emitted in the TSV and still deliberately IGNORED by the scale
  runner.** The July-vs-August argument is untouched: wall time counts every *other* process, and
  one run read `phase:parse` at **×5.03 then ×1.78 across a DOUBLING ladder** — preemption, not a
  curve of any shape.
- ⚠ **It is still an INSTRUMENT, not a gate**, exactly as the memory columns are. No verdict, no
  exponent fit, no residual, no NOISY: `scale-test` exits **0** whatever the numbers say, and a
  non-zero exit still means the **RUN broke**. A third column is a third thing to READ, not a thing
  to pass.
- ⚠ **It does NOT cure the OTHER blindness this file records — a corpus that cannot express the
  feature.** A Δ0 from a managed-free or generics-free corpus is still *"the instrument's blind
  spot, not the cost"*, and the cure for that is the scale-corpus catch-up, not this column. **Two
  different blind spots; do not credit one with the other's fix.**

⇒ **WHY IT HAD TO EXIST — the receipts are all in this file.** Every one of these is a measured
quadratic that **allocates nothing**, so the memory-only instrument read it as **Δ0**:

- **the op-insertion quadratic inside the float-across-calls rung** — `positionInBlock` +
  `Array.insert` + `shiftBlockSeqs`, fitted **`16.0n + 6.59n²`**, **68% of the whole compile at
  N=1024**, and stated there in its own words as *"allocation-free, so `scale-test` is structurally
  blind to it"*;
- **`regalloc:splitting` at ×3.9 then ×5.0 per doubling, ~98% of the compile** (the cascade rung's
  filing) — *"the strongest Workstream-O candidate on the board"*;
- **`requireInterfaceForParse`**, whose two arms allocate **identically to the digit, 1,417,523 both
  ways**, against a **+24.15 ms** parse delta;
- **`getBlockByIdIn`**'s per-guard-site linear scan — *"O(sites × blocks) in TIME, allocating
  NOTHING"*;
- **the per-instantiation generic gates** (`allocsΔ0`, measured **×2.36 → ×3.59 converging on ×4**),
  one of the two cascade duals whose closing commit (`4c4524b45` / `e306c562a`) says it outright —
  ***"'0 corpus hits' measured the instrument's blind spot, not the cost."***

⚠ **NOT on that list, and the exclusion is the point:** the float-across-calls quadratic's own
headline was hidden by the **CORPUS**, not by the memory-only column — the `floatSpill` knob was
**4**, few enough that every float took a register and no split happened, and it went **4 → 12** in
the fixing commit. Its allocations were never flat once the path was exercised (base
**1,275,640 → 80,849,418**). **That is the corpus blind spot wearing the same clothes, and O4 does
not touch it.**

⇒ **WHAT IT CHANGES FOR THE LIST BELOW.** Entries filed as unmeasurable-in-principle are marked
**⟲ RE-MEASURABLE (O4)** in place. **Their findings, numbers and attributions are unchanged** — a
measurement does not stop being true because a second way to take it appeared. What changed is that
each named RE-MEASURE TRIGGER can now be **pulled on the ladder** instead of waited for.

### Measured debt the trend log carries — revisit ONLY if the named trigger fires

`scale-test` and the per-type/per-scope tables have flagged these as **linear-in-practice**: real terms
that only bend under a specific future change. Each is filed with its measurement and its re-measure
trigger, not chased (a superlinearity you can *trigger* today is fixed, not filed):

- **⬜ `substituteValuesInFunc` RE-BOXES EVERY OP OF A FUNCTION THAT FOLDED AN IDENTITY — 448,127 allocations at rung 5, LINEAR (×1.97), and the cure would be a product term.** Filed 2026-08-26 by EC3's optimizer, measured by disabling the substitution outright. `remapStdOpUses` constructs a new boxed `StdOp` whether or not any operand moved; skipping unchanged ops needs a per-op "reads a substituted value" test, and the only allocation-free use enumerator (`collectStdOpUses`) writes a bit column that cannot be cleared per op in less than O(values) — clearing only the substituted ids is O(ops × substitutions), the shape the optimizer exists to remove. **Re-measure trigger:** anything that raises identities-per-function — a machine-generated enum-heavy corpus, or an inliner merging many small functions into one (R6). The re-run is `scale-test`'s `phase:foldConstOperands` column against EC3's row.
- **⬜ `inlineManagedPrimitives`' PER-SITE SPLIT CARRIES A Σ(B−pₖ) PRODUCT TERM THAT READS LINEAR — BECAUSE OF THREE FACTS ABOUT WHERE THE SITES ARE, NOT BECAUSE THE TERM IS ABSENT.** Filed 2026-08-25 by EC1's optimizer. `splitBlockInPlace(head, pos + 1)` copies the tail of the block into the continuation at every carve, so K sites in a block of B ops cost Σ(B−pₖ) ≈ K·B/2 — the shape `InsertRangeChecks.splitChainEnd` was built to avoid. MEASURED on `Testing/ladders/genmanagedsites.sh` (`onefunc`, n = 32/64/128/256 sites straight-line in ONE function; the scale corpus cannot express the axis — `ownedSiteBlock` wraps every group in an `if`): allocations **×1.99 ×1.99 ×2.00**, bytes ×2.07 ×2.10 ×2.06, where the product term would read ×4. Linear-in-practice because (1) the three throwing entries arrive as a `tryCall` whose flag is tested at once, so the call is its block's LAST op and the split moves nothing; (2) `__managed_get_unchecked` has exactly one emission site (`Parser.parseForStatement`'s header); (3) `__managed_count` is rewritten in place. **Re-measure trigger:** a sixth inlined primitive that carves MID-block, or any pass that merges a throwing call's blocks; the re-run is `genmanagedsites.sh onefunc`. ⚠ RE-MEASURED 2026-08-26 (EC3): `__managed_get_unchecked` carve sites per self-compile went **0 → 883** once every `for x in <Array>` took the index loop — the emission site is still one, but the per-compile carve count is no longer negligible; `onefunc` re-run recorded in EC3's row. The splitter's header states this in place of the argument it used to carry (which did not follow from its premise).
- **⬜ ONE `MethodReceiver` PER MEMBER-ACCESS SITE — 0.034%, AND THE NAMED FIX WAS DECLINED ON
  CLARITY GROUNDS** (D2 rung, 2026-07-29). A/B with both binaries rebuilt in one worktree:
  **+146 / +306 / +626 / +1,266 / +2,546 / +5,106** allocations, ratios **×2.10 ×2.05 ×2.02 ×2.01
  ×2.01** against a doubling ladder ⇒ **strictly linear**, one bundle per site. Attribution is exact
  rather than argued: the whole-module delta **equals `phase:parse`'s delta to the unit** at every

  fields. **0.034% of rung 5.** The implementer named the fix and it removes 100% of it: flatten
  `MethodReceiver` into seven positional parameters. **Declined by the coordinator, and the reviewer

- **⬜ `tokensHoldDirective` RE-SCANS EVERY TOKEN OF EVERY FILE TO ANSWER A QUESTION THE LEXER KNOWS

  mode) to save a rescan. **The shipped tier split is the right one: `fmt` reads `queryTokens`, the
  compiler reads `queryActiveTokens`.** (2) *"Fuse the pre-scan into the filter and copy lazily"*
  **saves nothing**: the gate exists so a directive-free file needs no array copy, and that file walks
  its tokens exactly ONCE either way. ⇒ the flag is the only route, and it is declined above. Note the
  failure mode if a flag were ever wrong is LOUD, not silent — a leaked directive token hits the parse

- **⬜ THE TWO UTF-8 DECODERS SHARE THREE LINES IN DIFFERENT ORDERS** (P1.8 Slice E review). `buffer + cursor`,
  `__utf8_cp_at`, `__utf8_len_at` — the genuinely coupled pair, left unfolded because folding renumbers values inside
  `body` and **moves committed goldens**. Three lines and a golden re-mint; the skeleton around them WAS folded
  (`emitStringWalkSkeleton`, byte-identical, sabotage reds 27).

- **⬜ A NO-ARGUMENT `s.trim()` COSTS THE COMPILER ~6.5× WHAT `s.trim(cs)` COSTS, PER SITE** (P1.8 Slice D
  optimizer, 2026-07-28). Measured on a private ladder at 1,024 call sites: **~3,266 allocations per site
  vs ~500** for the explicit form (4.24M vs the control's 0.90M), because the parser **inlines the whole
  7-member default preset at every site** rather than calling a shared entry point. **Strictly LINEAR in
  sites** — ×1.83…×1.97 per doubling — so it is a constant factor and NOT the fix mandate. **Named cure:**
  a runtime `__cs_default()` entry point, which collapses the per-site expansion to a call.
  **Re-measure trigger:** any rung that adds another no-argument `CharacterSet`-defaulted method (the
  obvious next ones are `trim`'s siblings gaining defaults, or `split`/`replace` taking a set), or any
  corpus that starts emitting `trim()` in bulk — at which point the constant is multiplied by a new
  surface and is worth the entry point.

- **⚠ RUNTIME COST, NOT COMPILER COST — a predefined `CharacterSet` is REBUILT ON EVERY CALL**
  (~1,068 ns and ~1,155 bytes of never-reclaimed slab per call, ≈ HALF the cost of a whole `trim()` of a
  9-byte string; P1.8 Slice D optimizer A/B against a hoisted-set control). It is a **constant** per call
  — the set has a fixed 7 members — and the blocker is that **shv2 has no module-level `static let` of a
  heap value**, so there is nowhere to cache it. **This is the THIRD and FOURTH firing of the slab
  trigger below** (a trim mints an owned result per call; the preset is rebuilt per call), after
  `for c in s` and `slice`-in-a-loop. Cured by the same recycling `__mm_free`; do not fix separately.

- **⭐⭐ `for c in s` ALLOCATES ONCE PER TRIP AND THE SLAB NEVER GIVES IT BACK — MEMORY IS LINEAR IN
  ITERATIONS, NOT LIVE DATA** (filed by P1.8 Slice B's optimizer, 2026-07-28). `MmRuntime` is a bump
  allocator with **no free list**, so a loop that mints a value per trip grows the working set without
  bound: **65,536 clusters → 11.6 MB · 262,144 → 97.1 MB · 1,048,576 → 398.7 MB**, at ~82 bytes per
  minted `Character`. ⚠ **It is NOT a leak** — every allocation is freed and no run exits 101 — the slab
  simply never reuses a slot. **TWO CONTROLS make it shv2's divergence rather than the algorithm's**:
  `count()` runs the SAME `__gr_end` scan minting nothing and stays **FLAT at 3.7 MB across a 4× data
  range**, and the C# bootstrap runs the same source in the same time (155.7 vs 156.4 ms) at **7.3 MB**.
  Not fixed here because the cure is a **recycling `__mm_free`** — which `Compiler/Runtime/MmRuntime.maxon:738`
  already anticipates in its own comment ("the day `__mm_free` returns a slot to a free list, the reused
  slot must be re-zeroed on alloc") — and that is a RUNTIME rung, not an optimizer's edit.
  **TRIGGER TO RE-MEASURE: any construct that allocates once per loop trip.** `for c in s` is the FIRST
  one the language has, which is exactly why this debt only became visible now.

- **⭐ THE SCALE CORPUS CONTAINS ZERO `for … in`, AND FOUR CONSECUTIVE RUNGS HAVE PAID FOR IT SEPARATELY**
  (measured by inventory, 2026-07-28). `--emit-corpus` at rung 5: `for … in` in any form **0**; `.count()`
  **1,024 sites, every one an Array/Set receiver**, not one String; `.bytes()` **0**; `'…'` tokens 53,766
  **of which 0 are in a value position** (all block labels). ⚠ P1.8 Slice A committed `Testing/ladders/genfor.sh`
  for precisely this hole and **the main corpus was never taught the construct**, so every later rung
  re-hit it. The tree now carries FOUR private ladders — `genfor.sh` (Slice A), `genborrow.sh` (E3070),
  `genstring.sh` (Slice C), `genstring-grapheme.sh` (Slice B) — plus upstream's function-value ladder, each
  built because the shared instrument could not express what its rung added. **That is an instrument
  problem, not five coincidences**, and it is why a Δ0 from `ScaleCorpus` is worth nothing until you have
  read what the corpus actually contains. ⚠ Note the trap runs BOTH ways: the corpus is *not* blind to
  `String` (756 `==` sites), so a neighbour of the shape reads non-zero and can be mistaken for coverage.

- **`__str_find` IS A NAIVE SEARCH WITH A GENUINE O(haystack × needle) TERM** (filed by P1.8 Slice C's
  optimizer, 2026-07-28). `Testing/ladders/genstring.sh <n> data-findquad` reads **×3.92 ×4.15 ×3.95 ×4.14**.
  ⚠ **It needs BOTH conditions at once**: a needle whose LENGTH SCALES WITH the haystack, *and* data
  self-similar enough to defeat the first-byte fast reject. A fixed needle is a constant factor —
  `data-find` reads **×2.04** — and it is measured LINEAR on every realistic shape including `split`
  (×2.04 over 16× segments) and `replace` (×1.96 over 16× matches), its two biggest consumers.
  **TRIGGER TO RE-MEASURE: a consumer that searches with a needle whose length grows with its input.**
  The fix is two-way/KMP. ⚠ **`stdlib/String.maxon`'s `findIn` — which BOTH reference compilers run —
  has the same shape**, so this is a shared property of the language's search, not an shv2 divergence.

- **`Parser.borrowSubjectIdOf` IS O(K²) IN DISTINCT BORROWED-AND-WRITTEN STORAGES IN ONE BODY** (filed by the
  E3070 rung's optimizer, 2026-07-28). A linear scan of the distinct-subject list, entered once per borrow
  mint and once per recorded write. Measured on `Testing/ladders/genborrow.sh`'s `subjects` mode:
  **×3.99 ×2.23 ×2.66 ×3.08** per doubling. Fitting `aK + bK²` over the top two rungs gives **a = 15,697,
  b = 36.2 ticks**, so the quadratic term does not equal the linear one below **K ≈ 434 distinct subjects in
  a single function body**. The scale corpus reaches 256 there (~2.4M ticks at rung 5, **~0.02% of the
  compile**); hand-written code reaches single digits. **TRIGGER TO RE-MEASURE: machine-generated code
  declaring hundreds of distinct arrays in one body.** Not fixed because both closures — 8 bytes on every
  `VarInfo`, or a per-function `Map` — tax every program to buy a term that is invisible on all of them.
  ⚠ Note what made it findable at all: the scale corpus was **NOT BLIND to this rung, it was NARROW**, which
  reads as coverage and is worse — it holds one borrow per subject and binds every accessor to a name, so
  every quadratic the rung could contain has degree 1 there and cannot appear. The purpose-built ladder is
  the instrument; the corpus's healthy non-zero was not evidence.

- **#124 — shv2's ARRAY ROSTER IS SHORT OF THE BOOTSTRAP'S, AND ITS EMPTY-SLOT SURFACE IS ONE FUNCTION WIDE.**
  Two residuals from the `Array.resize` fix (`98834dd2e`), both disclosed rather than papered over.
  **(a) THE REMEDY LIST IS ASYMMETRIC.** E3106 refuses `resize`-to-grow on a managed element type in BOTH
  compilers, but shv2 synthesizes neither `growFilled` nor `truncate`, so its diagnostic can only offer `push`
  where the bootstrap offers all three. A user told to shrink a managed array in shv2 has **no supported call** —
  `resize` is now refused and `truncate` does not exist. **5 cases in `specs-shv2/array-slots.md` are
  `disabled-test`** with the missing mechanism named in each.
  **(b) `emptySlot` COLLAPSES INTO `indexOutOfBounds`.** The bootstrap now distinguishes them — that was the second
  defect the fix uncovered, and the reason `CompileTimings` died reporting *"phase index OOB for 'load'"* about an
  index that was perfectly in range. shv2's `emitLoadElemAndOkReturn` still reports a NULL slot through the same
  `emitOobReturn` a real range violation uses, so 4 of those 5 disabled cases are this. **A wrong error code sent a
  reader hunting an index bug for a null-slot bug once already; it will again.**
  **(c) AND THE CHECK LIVES ONLY IN `get`, IN BOTH.** Measured, not inferred: `for x in arr` over a sparse array
  panics *nil pointer or invalid memory access*, and `arr.pop()` gives *mm_incref called with NULL pointer* in
  `SlotArray.pop`. E3106 closes the only ORDINARY route to a sparse array, so these are now reachable only through
  raw `managed.setLength` or opaque-generic code — which is why this is filed and not chased.
  **Re-measure trigger:** shv2 gaining `growFilled`/`truncate` (which would let the 5 specs re-enable and is the
  natural moment to widen the read surface), or any new route that can open a slot without going through `resize`.

- **#122 — `phase:parse` IS Θ(MUTABLE BINDINGS × CONSTRUCTS) ON THE REAL CORPUS, AND IT IS A RUNG RATHER THAN AN EDIT.**
  ⭐ **This is the corpus's parse superlinearity — NOT nesting depth**, and the distinction was measured, not reasoned.
  `parseWhileStatement` (`Parser.maxon:10925`) and `assignedBindingsIn` (`:11463`) each loop
  `for k in 0 upto self.mutableVars.count()` per construct, asking one membership question per binding.
  The corpus's `d_blocks.maxon` is ONE function with **518 mutable vars in scope**, so that is **414,400 tests at
  rung 2 and 26.5 MILLION at rung 5**. **Measured:** halving the O(depth × tokens) term (`4110c7d00`) left the corpus
  parse ratios UNCHANGED — ×1.91 ×2.14 ×2.39 ×2.75 ×3.03 against a baseline ×1.94 ×2.16 ×2.43 ×2.74 ×2.99 — which is
  what proves the depth term is not what this corpus spends its parse time on. ⚠ **AN ATTEMPTED FIX WAS A ×3.45
  REGRESSION AND WAS BACKED OUT:** a per-file `name → assignment-sites` index with binary search went flat on the
  depth ladder, passed every gate, and then measured ×3.45 at rung 5 — because it replaced a small per-construct set
  (one hash, one probe per test) with a structure whose per-test cost MULTIPLIED this same Θ(V×C). **A ladder-flat,
  corpus-worse change is a regression, and only running BOTH caught it.** The cure for this and for the remaining
  depth term is the same one thing: **carried sets computed BOTTOM-UP over the construct tree** — each construct's set
  is its own direct sites ∪ its children's memoized sets — making both the scan and the per-binding loop O(Σ|set|).
  **It is a RUNG because it changes the ORDER a phi set is built in, and the goldens pin that order** (`LoopPhiVar`'s
  header calls the ordering load-bearing). `matchingEndOf` from `4110c7d00` is the piece it builds on.
  **Re-measure trigger:** any corpus knob that raises mutable-vars-in-scope, or an inliner that fuses functions.

- **✅ #123 — THE `Map` PROBE TRAP — CLOSED 2026-07-26. Instance, class AND every named site are done; nothing is
  left as debt, and the five maps' verdicts were MEASURED rather than assumed.** The trap: `stdlib` `Map` is
  open-addressed with linear probing and `int.hash()` is the **identity**
  (`stdlib/PrimitiveExtensions.maxon:3-5`), so a key's home slot was `id and (capacity-1)`. Insert two contiguous id
  runs *interleaved* and the high run wraps onto the low run's slots, fusing them into one cluster every insert
  walks. **Measured** on the encoder's per-function block-offset map: probes per insert were **exactly
  `capacity/4 + 2/3`** (3.33 at cap 16 … 512.67 at cap 2048), collapsing to **1.00** the instant capacity first
  exceeded the id range — 171.44 probes/insert against 1.00 for the same keys sorted. Three things closed it:
  - **The INSTANCE** — `a78d17c35` made the encoder's table two pre-sized arrays (the key WAS the index).
  - **The CLASS** — ⚠ **the mixer this entry used to say was "DELIBERATELY NOT DONE" HAS BEEN DONE**, in
    `4def53ced`: `spreadHash` (MurmurHash3 `fmix32`, `stdlib/Interfaces.maxon:105`) now avalanches a hash at all six
    slot derivations in `Map`/`Set`, so **no key ORDER can cluster and the trap is unreachable for any key shape**.
    The iteration-order risk this entry declined it on was *measured*, not reasoned about, and is zero:
    `specs-shv2/fragments/` empty on two targets, the bootstrap's fragment diff byte-identical, all 16 `Map`/`Set`
    iteration sites swept, `verify-warm-rebuild` PASS.
  - **The SITES** — the two remaining `BlockId`-keyed maps became dense tables (2026-07-26).
    `SemanticCheck.buildBlockByIdMap` and `StdToWasm.BlockDispatchMap` are gone; both now read one
    `BlockIndexById` from `IrModule.blockIndexById` (the inverse of `func.blockRefs`), an instantiation of the new
    generic `BlockKeyedTable` (`Compiler/IR/`) that `BlockOffsetTable` also instantiates — **one array-pair-with-
    presence-column, not three copies**. −1,536 `semanticCheck` allocations (−68%) and −92% of its bytes on
    `Testing/ladders/genawait.sh 24 400`; −6,864 `encode` allocations on the wasm rung3 corpus. `scale-test` sees
    NEITHER (no `async` in the corpus, and `compileRung` always builds for the host) — its own Δ0 for them is the
    corpus blind spot, and the ladder is committed so the numbers can be re-run.
  ⭐ **AND THE MIXER DOES NOT MAKE A DENSE `Map` FINE — IT MAKES IT ~3× WORSE, WHICH IS WHY THE PER-SITE "TIDY
  O(n)" WAS STILL WORTH TAKING.** Replaying the real key sequences of a 2,808-function corpus through `Map`'s exact
  algorithm, both maps' keys arrive **perfectly ascending in 2,808/2,808 and 24/24 instances** — the interleaving
  run comes from the register allocator's critical-edge split, which neither site sees — and that is the case an
  identity hash gets perfect: **1.000 probes/insert, against 3.088 / 3.062 under `spreadHash`**.
  **The three `ValueId`-keyed maps were MEASURED AND LEFT, and each is a closure rather than a residual** — the
  trap needs an interleaved union of contiguous runs, not merely int keys, and replaying their real key sequences
  says none of them has one. In every case the arrival order costs **exactly what the SORTED order costs**, which
  is the definitive test, because the trap is order-induced:
  - `StdToWasm.DependentLhsMap` — 1,065 instances, 39,137 keys, largest 16,902. **Ascending in 1,065/1,065.**
    1.948 probes/insert under the identity hash, 1.948 sorted (3.212 under `spreadHash`, sparse keys).
  - `StdToX64Conversion.CmpPredMap` — 1,101 instances, 20,222 keys. Ascending in 1,098/1,101; the three
    exceptions cost nothing (2.583 arrival vs **2.583** sorted in aggregate; worst single instance 4.957, from
    SPARSITY, not clustering). It is also a genuinely sparse subset of the value space that supports `remove`, so
    a dense column would allocate per-function for a handful of entries.
  - `Parser.ValueInstanceAliasMap` — ascending in 2/2 instances, 2.203 arrival vs 2.203 sorted. The parser mints
    `ValueId`s monotonically in one forward pass and records the alias where the value is created, so ascending is
    structural. ⚠ **It is also ITERATED** (`Parser.maxon:6925`, feeding `recordFunctionRangeChecks`), so converting
    it would change an order that reaches a recorded artifact — a real hazard for no measured gain.
  **Nothing to re-measure**: the mixer makes the class unreachable regardless of key order, so an inliner giving
  Maxon-tier ids a second run can no longer trigger it, and the two sites that would have felt it most are arrays.

- **#106 — the COW detach is an unconditional call on the ARRAY HOT PATH (a constant factor, deliberately taken).**
  Every `push`/`reserve`/`resize`/`insert`/`append` now pays a `__arr_cow_detach` call that no-ops for an ordinary
  owned array, and `set`/`clear`/`remove`/`pop` pay it directly; a `push` onto a literal allocates and copies TWICE
  (detach, then grow). **Measured** (optimizer, 2026-07-22, 6-padding sweep): a candidate hoisting the guard to the
  call sites won **−18% on `reserve`** (spreads disjoint, faster 6/6) and −7.5% on `set`. **REJECTED, and the reason
  is the point:** a hoisted site guard tests `capacity < 0`, but a Slice-B shared HEAP buffer has `capacity >= 0`, so
  the site would skip the call and **Slice B's detach would never fire** — a slice-A optimization silently defeating
  the next slice. The unconditional placement is also what makes the gate structural rather than a checklist.
  **Re-measure trigger: after Slice B lands** (when the detach test has its second arm and the two questions are
  genuinely one), or if array-heavy code shows up in a profile. ⭐ **The better lever is SHRINK-WRAPPING** —
  12 of the 18 instructions on the detach's fast path are frame, and 6 of those (`push`/`pop` of `rbx`/`r12`/`r13`)
  serve only the cold arm; sinking callee-saved saves into the blocks that clobber them pays off across every emitted
  runtime function with a hot early-out (`__arr_get`/`__arr_set`, the `__str_*` and `__mm_*` families). ⚠ Not free:
  `X64GtRuntime.maxon:85-95` hard-couples `calleeSavedOrder` to `__gt_spawn`'s initial frame behind a live
  `panic("GT frame drift: …")`, so a variable frame shape must be reconciled with the green-thread context switch;
  frame pointers stay mandatory (`__gt_morestack`).
  ⚠⚠ **METHODOLOGY, and it invalidated this rung's first answer: emitted-code benchmarks here swing ±30% ON CODE
  LAYOUT ALONE.** The first A/B read "−16% push, −22% clone" and **both were noise** — proven by a `clone` CONTROL the
  change could not possibly affect, which still moved −22%. `emitForwardCopy` is a byte-at-a-time loop with 3 branches
  per byte, so it is acutely BTB/alignment-sensitive. **Require a padding sweep with disjoint spreads before believing
  any emitted-code delta, and never A/B on a benchmark dominated by that copy loop.**
- **#24(a) — `SplitLiveRanges` is O(blocks × K²)**, K = simultaneously-live owned values per block; measured
  K max 8, mean 0.16 over 2,445 fns ⇒ linear. (A separate quadratic — full liveness re-sweep per split —
  was already retired via `ReachCache`.) Re-measure trigger = an **INLINER** (shv2 has none).
- **scale-corpus catch-up — `RangeCheckEmitter` locates each guard site's block with `getBlockByIdIn` (`IrModule.maxon:361`), a LINEAR SCAN of `func.blockRefs`, called once per guard site (`InsertRangeChecks.maxon:329`)** ⇒ **O(sites × blocks) in TIME, allocating NOTHING**, so **no rung of this ladder could ever show it** — the manifest's own MEASURES-MEMORY-ONLY blind spot, stated by the instrument about itself. ⟲ **RE-MEASURABLE (O4, 2026-07-25): that sentence is no longer true** — see the tail of this entry. Surfaced because this rung took `phase:insertRangeChecks` from INERT to ACTIVE (the old corpus contained no narrow-range cast, only FULL-range aliases that `rangeIsFull` refuses to guard, so the pass did literally nothing — 72 allocs / 2,395 bytes flat at every rung, for the ladder's entire history). Independently re-measured by the review, which agreed. The phase is 0.066% of rung-7 bytes and its guard-SITE count is FIXED at one per rung, so the growing term is the per-function scan over `module.functions` (`InsertRangeChecks.maxon:83-86`), whose `project.rangeChecks.contains(func.name)` probe now hashes against a non-empty map. **RE-MEASURE TRIGGER: many narrow-range casts inside LARGE functions** — a machine-generated program, or a real one once ranged types are used densely. **CURE:** an id→block index on `IrFunction`, single-writer. ⚠ Note the shape it shares with the `requireInterfaceForParse` entry below: both are per-site linear scans over a per-function list, both allocation-free, and **both were therefore invisible to the only trend artifact this project keeps** — which was an argument for the runtime/time instrument that did not exist yet, not for a knob. ⟲ **RE-MEASURABLE (O4, 2026-07-25) — THAT INSTRUMENT NOW EXISTS.** `scale-test` carries a per-phase **CPU-TIME** column, so this entry's trigger can be **pulled on the ladder** rather than waited for: build the many-narrow-casts-in-large-functions corpus and read `phase:insertRangeChecks` in CPU ticks, where an O(sites × blocks) term shows as ×4 per doubling against the memory columns' ×2. **The measurement above is unchanged and still stands.** ⚠ Read it against the CPU column's noise band (a few percent): the ×2-vs-×4 question clears it by 100%, a constant-factor claim would not.
- **P1.7a 2b-ii — `Parser.requireInterfaceForParse` resolves a `where`-constraint interface by LINEAR SCAN over the current file's `artifact.interfaces` after missing the builtin table**, making witness dispatch **O(dispatch sites × interfaces declared in the same file)** — unchanged by 2b-ii, which merely measured it. ⚠ **TIME-ONLY and allocation-free, so `scale-test` STRUCTURALLY COULD NOT SEE IT** — the class the corpus manifest warns about in its own words (*"a cost that re-walks tokens or chases pointers but allocates little will read FLAT in these columns even when it is quadratic in time"*). Isolated with the hit's INDEX as the only variable (`Digest` declared last vs first — same program, same N interfaces, same N sites): **allocations identical at 1,417,523 both ways**, parse ratios ×2.52 vs ×2.19, and **+24.15 ms of a +27.05 ms whole-compile delta at N=1024**, everything else inside noise. **MEASURED LINEAR-IN-PRACTICE: max 17 interfaces in any single file** across `maxon-shv2`, `stdlib`, `maxon-selfhosted` and `specs-shv2`, and the scan only walks the CURRENT file's artifact ⇒ K ≤ 17, the `SplitLiveRanges` K² situation. **RE-MEASURE TRIGGER: a machine-generated source file, or any rung that lands many protocol interfaces in ONE artifact.** ⟲ **RE-MEASURABLE (O4, 2026-07-25) — AND THIS ENTRY IS THE CASE THAT ARGUED FOR THE COLUMN.** *"Allocations identical at 1,417,523 both ways"* against *"+24.15 ms"* is the exact shape a memory-only instrument reports as Δ0; `scale-test` now carries a per-phase **CPU-TIME** column, so the trigger is **pullable on the ladder** — put many interfaces in one artifact and read `phase:parse` in CPU ticks. **Every number above is unchanged and still stands**; K ≤ 17 across the whole tree remains the reason this is filed rather than fixed. **CURE:** an index beside `artifact.interfaces` with a single writer — which would also remove `builtinInterface`'s construct-on-every-lookup (it builds a fresh `IrInterface` per call, the same constructor-as-lookup shape as `builtinOrderingEnum`), folding in this file's existing "memoize `builtinInterface`" note. ⟲ **SECOND AXIS, MEASURED BY 2b-v's OPTIMIZER (2026-07-28) — same family, different dimension, same cure.** The entry above measures INTERFACES-PER-FILE (K ≤ 17). `IrInterface.interfaceMethodIndex` (`IrInterface.maxon:302`) is the METHODS-PER-INTERFACE twin: also a linear scan, also run once per witness-dispatch site, so witness dispatch is **O(sites × methods-on-that-interface)** as well. Isolated with the target method's POSITION as the only variable (same program, moved first→last): `phase:parse` **+13.7% at M=D=256, +39.3% at 512, +36.2% at 1024** (min of 5). ⚠ **THE OPTIMIZER EXPLICITLY DECLINED TO CLAIM THE EXPONENT** and was right to: the isolated delta grew ×5.52 then ×1.90 where a clean D×M term predicts ×4.00, so the measurement shows the term EXISTS and cannot show its SHAPE. **FILED, NOT FIXED, on a coordinator-verified trigger: the widest interface anywhere in the tree is FOUR methods** (`stdlib/Interfaces.maxon`'s `Hashable` has one; the widest in `specs-shv2` is 4), and the effect needs a few hundred — ~64× beyond anything that exists, so it is not triggerable on realistic input. **RE-MEASURE TRIGGER: an interface wider than a few dozen methods** (a machine-generated one, or a protocol that grows). **CURE: index `IrInterface.methods` by name** — the same single-writer index the axis above wants, which is why both belong to ONE entry rather than two.
- **P1.7 deep-clone — `noteClonerUsage` needs-fixpoint is O(passes × total-types)**, passes = depth of the
  deepest cloner-dependency chain (`ArrayRuntime.maxon`, 3b-vi-b-α). Measured LINEAR on realistic input
  (optimizer, 2026-07-23, hand-built managed Corpus A — scale-test's corpus is managed-free so it CANNOT see
  this: ~5015 allocs per added managed type at nesting depth D≈1); bends to superlinear only when deep-clone
  NESTING depth scales with program size (Corpus B, a 256-deep managed struct chain: `unattributed` allocs
  ×6.44 per doubling). A structural DUAL of the pre-existing destructor-needs fixpoint `closeDestructorNeeds`
  (`MmRuntime.maxon`), which carries the IDENTICAL quadratic (measured 175,415 unattributed at D=256 with the
  clone removed — so this is not a regression the rung introduced, it inherited the destructor's shape).
  Re-measure trigger = a machine-generated deeply-nested managed type that gets deep-cloned. Fix, if ever
  warranted = ONE shared worklist helper for BOTH the destructor and cloner needs-closures (O(types+edges)),
  which single-sources the dual too — NOT a clone-only fork.
  ⚠ **NOT an O4 case, and the distinction matters: this one is ALLOCATION-shaped, and its blind spot is the
  CORPUS** (managed-free), not the memory-only column. The CPU-time column does not cure it; corpus coverage
  does. ✅ **And it is CLOSED** — re-measured at the trigger it names (cloner **×2.75 → ×3.82**, destructor
  **×2.94 → ×3.83** at D=64→512, so *"bends only on machine-generated 256-deep chains"* was wrong), and the
  ONE shared worklist this entry prescribed shipped as `Compiler/Runtime/CascadeNeeds.maxon` (`4c4524b45`,
  closing note `e306c562a`; after: ×1.93 / ×1.96). Detail lives in the P1.7 status row; kept here for the
  measurement and the lesson.
- **P1.7 opaque-copy — the front-end per-instantiation GATES scan ALL generic instances per call-site.**
  `genericTypeFieldHasUncopyableInstantiation` (copy-reject gate, `SignatureIndex.maxon:3098`, 3b-vi-b-β) and
  its shipped twin `genericTypeFieldHasManagedInstantiation` (opaque-field-reassign drop gate, `:3073`, Finding
  A) each `for id in 0 upto genericInstances.count()` base-name `.equals` per call-site → **O(sites × total-
  instances)**. Measured TIME-only (optimizer, 2026-07-23, managed-opaque corpus: copied-vs-nocopy `parse` grows
  ×2.5/doubling, quadratic ≈40–75 ns/K²) — but `nameOf` borrows and `.equals` doesn't allocate, so it was
  **INVISIBLE to scale-test** (allocsΔ0). ⟲ **RE-MEASURABLE (O4, 2026-07-25):** the per-phase CPU-TIME column
  sees exactly this shape, so the trigger below is pullable on the ladder. ⚠ **And this entry's own verdict was
  re-measured and OVERTURNED** — see the P1.7 status row: *"linear-in-practice (0 corpus hits)"* was the
  instrument's blind spot, the gates measured **×2.36 → ×3.59 converging on ×4**, and the shared by-base-id index
  this entry prescribed **SHIPPED** (`4c4524b45`, closing note `e306c562a`). Kept here for the measurement and
  the lesson. Linear-in-practice: **0 occurrences** in the scale corpus or shv2's own
  source; sub-ms at realistic K (tens of generic copy/reassign-container types); bends visibly only at K in the
  hundreds (~32 ms at K=800, machine-generated). Re-measure trigger = a program with hundreds of generic types
  that copy/reassign opaque type-parameter fields. Fix = a shared **by-base-name index** on the generic-instance
  registry benefiting BOTH gates (do NOT fork one gate — the twin is a shipped path).
- **#28 — the corpus hardcodes struct F=2**, hiding `StructLayout.indexOfField`'s O(F²) scan; measured F
  max 22 mean 4.14 over 166 real type decls ⇒ linear (programs add TYPES, not width). Re-measure needs a
  field-count corpus knob (a machine-generated wide type).
- **#32 — the E2027 duplicate-pattern check is O(P²)** in one match's hand-written arm count P; whole-program
  linear for bounded arms, quadratic only in a degenerate single-giant-match. Kept deliberately (a `Set` = a
  heap object per match to save a bounded scan).
- **#30 — the corpus is BLIND to instance methods AND `match`** (no knob emits either), so the optimizer
  measured ZERO allocation there; both paths are O(1)/O(fields) by inspection. Fold a method knob + a match
  knob in together.
- **#24(b) — post-pipeline runtime installs are billed to NO phase** (`installMmRuntime`/`installGtRuntime`/
  `installStringRuntime`/the destructor cascades run after `pipeline.run()`, outside every `PhaseProbe`), so
  phases don't sum to total; a constant ~316-alloc delta shows as `unattributed`. Constant, not superlinear.
- **#76 — the 14-register x64 pool refuses a 16-live-value interpolation-in-a-loop body (E5001)**, which
  restricts `capturing-closure-bound-outside-loop-called-inside` to wasm. Proven closure-INDEPENDENT (the
  same body with a plain `let r = i + 5` E5001s identically) — the "refuse the search" thesis firing, not a
  bug; x64 env-drop timing is covered by the `-rebound-in-loop`/`-called-from-nested-block` siblings.

- **`selfhost-distance` (the compass)** — ❌ **CUT 2026-07-13.** It was sold as "the ranked
  TOP-UNSUPPORTED table IS the roadmap," but the roadmap is ordered by *reasons* a frequency table
  cannot discover (dictionary-passing forces the descriptor drop path before `Array`; `String` is
  a runtime-gated builtin). **We know what we need to implement.** Its real price, re-measured: a
  parser recovery mode + making `panic()` recoverable at **626** sites (the plan guessed 148, and
  projected ~600 only by *mid*-ladder; we hit it at the *end of the scalar core*). It buys a
  number, not a feature. `SelfhostDistance.maxon` was never written — the cut is docs-only.
  **The Phase 1 gate is the mitigation:** it answers "does shv2 compile real Maxon?" on 704 lines
  instead of 21k, which is most of what the compass promised for none of its cost.
- **The `panic()` audit** and **parser recovery mode** — VOID with the compass. shv2 needs neither.
- **The `spec-test` runner** — ✅ **SHIPPED** (`72ffe87a9`). `Compiler.maxon` grew `compileSource()`
  + `CompileOutcome` (returns `project.diagnostics` instead of printing them — `Diagnostic.render()`
  already emits the exact `error EXXXX:` wire format `maxoncstderr` compares against). **Do NOT
  port v1's 7,699-line harness.**
- **Rewriting shv2's core-violating sites** — VOID. Closures and conditional conformance are *in
  core*; the sites are the tests.
